{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Okayama Prefecture, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=November 2019}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Kibitsu Jinja
吉備津神社 | image = Kibitsu Jinja 10 cropped.jpg | caption = [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]] (1425), a [[National Treasures of Japan|National Treasure]] {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|14.4|N|133|51|2.2|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title, inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = Kibitsu Jinja | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 931 Kibitsu, Kita-ku, Okayama-shi, Okayama-ken 701-1341 | website = {{official|1=https://kibitujinja.com}} | architecture_style = | festivals = Second Sunday in May and October 15th each year | leadership = | footnotes = }} {{nihongo|'''Kibitsu Jinja'''|吉備津神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in the Kibitsu neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' (first shrine) of former [[Bitchū Province]]. The shrine’s main festivals are held on the second Sunday in May and October 15th each year.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} ==Overview== The Kibitsu Jinja is located in the western part of Okayama city, facing north at the northwestern foot of Mount Kibi-Nakayama (elevation 175 meters) on the border between former [[Bizen Province]] and Bitchū Province. The mountain has been worshipped as a [[sacred mountain]] from ancient times, and both the Kibitsu Jinja and [[Kibitsuhiko Shrine|Kibitsuhiko Jinja]] are located at its northeastern foot. Kibitsu Jinja was originally the general guardian of [[Kibi Province]], but due to the division of Kibi Province into three provinces, it became the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of Bitchū, and ''[[bunrei]]'' from this shrine created the ''ichinomiya'' of Bizen Province (Kibitsuhiko Jinja) and [[Bingo Province]] (Kibitsu Shrine). The [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]], which was re-built by [[Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]], is a [[National Treasures of Japan|National Treasure]] and the sole exemplar of the ''[[kibitsu-zukuri]]'' style of [[Japanese architecture|architecture]], although the [[Dō (architecture)|Soshidō]] of [[Hokekyō-ji (Ichikawa)|Hokekyō-ji]] is now believed to have been modeled thereon.{{cite web |url=http://www.aisf.or.jp/~jaanus/deta/k/kibitsuzukuri.htm |title=Kibitsu-zukuri |publisher=[[Japanese Architecture and Art Net Users System]] |access-date=4 May 2011}}{{cite book |title=Architectural Preservation in Japan |author=Larsen, Knut Einar |publisher=[[ICOMOS]] International Wood Committee |year=1994 |pages=121–5 |isbn=82-519-1432-9}} In addition, the three shrine buildings are designated as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]], and a special Shinto ritual "Narukama Shinto" is famous. === Mizuko and Sorei syncretism === The Shrine has a unique dual worship of [[Sorei]] or ancestral spirits alongside [[Mizuko kuyō]]{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=239}} or cults of miscarried babies. The shrine started as a place for the Kibi clan. It has the clan's ancestors as gods. This gives the shrine a pure and protective feel. The ancestors are seen as good and helpful spirits. This is how the shrine connects with [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] means the souls of babies who died early or were not born.{{Rp|page=239}} The shrine places the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] shrine next to the ancestor shrine. It also uses running water. This setup has several meanings:{{Rp|page=239}} # The water purifies the souls of [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] is linked to water.{{Rp|page=239}} # Being near the ancestor shrine suggests these souls become kind and protective spirits.{{Rp|page=239}} # As protective spirits, the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] guard those who remember them.{{Rp|page=239}} This way, the Kibitsu Shrine uses its ties to the Kibi clan. It creates a respectful place for [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. It links them to the shrine's ancestral and protective gods.{{Rp|page=239}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Kibitsu Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]]'''|吉備津彦命|}}, the son of [[Emperor Kōrei]] and conqueror of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]] and founder of the [[Kibi clan]] * {{nihongo|'''Mitomowake-no-mikoto'''| 御友別命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Nakatsuhiko-no-mikoto| 仲彦命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Chichihaya-hime-no-mikoto'''|千々速比売命|}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Yamato-totohimomoso-hime-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日百襲姫命 |}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosasukatawake-no-mikoto'''| 日子刺肩別命|}}, elder brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosashikatawake-no-mikoto'''| 彦刺肩別命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hiko same ma no mikoto'''|彦寤間命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Wakahiko Takekibitsu Hikono-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日稚屋媛命|}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko ==History== The origins of Kibitsu Jinja are uncertain. According to the shrine's legend, it is located at the site of Kibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto's residence, where he died at the age of 281, and was buried on the summit of the mountain. Afterwards, the residence was turned into a shrine, possibly by his fifth generation descendent Narumi Kaya, or by [[Emperor Nintoku]], who visited [[Kibi Province]] where he built several shrines to commemorate Kibitsuhiko. However, the shrine does not appear in any historical documentation until the late [[Heian period]], until entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'' dated 847 and the ''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' dated 852. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'' it was given the rank of {{nihongo|''Myojin Taisha''|名神大社||}} and the rank of ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of the province. From the [[Kamakura period|Kamakura]] through the [[Sengoku period]], was revered by the samurai, and there were frequent restorations of the shrine and donations of territory. {{Citation needed|date=November 2023}} During the [[Edo period]], the shrine's land became smaller. However, it still got a special land grant from the shogunate. This grant was for 160 koku of rice every year. There was a busy market near the shrine. People also visited teahouses and inns there. Inside the shrine area, there was a theater and a brothel. The shrine was a busy place along the [[San'yōdō|San’yodō]] for travellers. This continued until the [[Meiji Restoration]]..{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=282}} After the [[Meiji Restoration]] in 1871, it was listed as a {{nihongo|National Shrine, 2nd rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Chusha}}, and is 1914 was promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial Shrine, 2nd rank|官幣中社|Kampei Chusha}}.{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese}}{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} The shrine is a ten-minute walk from [[Kibitsu Station]] on the [[JR West]] [[Kibi Line]]. ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *''[[Honden]]'' and ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]]'', [[Muromachi period]], built in 1390 and relocated their present locations in 1425.The main shrine has a ''Kibitsu-zukuri'' style roof, which consists of two [[East Asian hip-and-gable roof|''Irimoya-zukuri'']] roof are lined up in front and behind. The influence of Buddhist architecture can be seen in many details of the structure.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2993 |title= 吉備津神社本殿及び拝殿|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine main hall and worship hall|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} ===Important Cultural Properties=== *{{nihongo|'''South Zuishinmon'''|南随神門||}}, [[Muromachi period]], built in 1357.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2994 |title=吉備津神社南随神門|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine South Zuijinmon|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} *{{nihongo|'''North Zuishinmon'''|北随神門||}}, [[Sengoku period]], built in 1543.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2995 |title=吉備津神社北随神門|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine North Zuijinmon|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} *{{nihongo|'''Okama-den'''|御釜殿||}}, [[Edo period]], built in 1612.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2996 |title= 吉備津神社御釜殿|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine Okamaden|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} *{{nihongo|'''Komainu'''|木造獅子狛犬||}}, one pair, late [[Kamakura Period|Kamakura]] to [[Nanboku-cho period]], Located to the east and west of the Honden.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/10545 |title= 木造獅子狛犬|trans-title=Mokuzō shishi komainu|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} ==Gallery== File:吉備津神社 御釜殿.JPG|Okamaden（ICP） File:Kibitsu Jinja Corridor 03.JPG|Cloister {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Okayama Prefecture, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=November 2019}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Kibitsu Jinja
吉備津神社 | image = Kibitsu Jinja 10 cropped.jpg | caption = [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]] (1425), a [[National Treasures of Japan|National Treasure]] {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|14.4|N|133|51|2.2|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title, inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = Kibitsu Jinja | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 931 Kibitsu, Kita-ku, Okayama-shi, Okayama-ken 701-1341 | website = {{official|1=https://kibitujinja.com}} | architecture_style = | festivals = Second Sunday in May and October 15th each year | leadership = | footnotes = }} {{nihongo|'''Kibitsu Jinja'''|吉備津神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in the Kibitsu neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' (first shrine) of former [[Bitchū Province]]. The shrine’s main festivals are held on the second Sunday in May and October 15th each year.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} ==Overview== The Kibitsu Jinja is located in the western part of Okayama city, facing north at the northwestern foot of Mount Kibi-Nakayama (elevation 175 meters) on the border between former [[Bizen Province]] and Bitchū Province. The mountain has been worshipped as a [[sacred mountain]] from ancient times, and both the Kibitsu Jinja and [[Kibitsuhiko Shrine|Kibitsuhiko Jinja]] are located at its northeastern foot. Kibitsu Jinja was originally the general guardian of [[Kibi Province]], but due to the division of Kibi Province into three provinces, it became the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of Bitchū, and ''[[bunrei]]'' from this shrine created the ''ichinomiya'' of Bizen Province (Kibitsuhiko Jinja) and [[Bingo Province]] (Kibitsu Shrine). The [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]], which was re-built by [[Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]], is a [[National Treasures of Japan|National Treasure]] and the sole exemplar of the ''[[kibitsu-zukuri]]'' style of [[Japanese architecture|architecture]], although the [[Dō (architecture)|Soshidō]] of [[Hokekyō-ji (Ichikawa)|Hokekyō-ji]] is now believed to have been modeled thereon.{{cite web |url=http://www.aisf.or.jp/~jaanus/deta/k/kibitsuzukuri.htm |title=Kibitsu-zukuri |publisher=[[Japanese Architecture and Art Net Users System]] |access-date=4 May 2011}}{{cite book |title=Architectural Preservation in Japan |author=Larsen, Knut Einar |publisher=[[ICOMOS]] International Wood Committee |year=1994 |pages=121–5 |isbn=82-519-1432-9}} In addition, the three shrine buildings are designated as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]], and a special Shinto ritual "Narukama Shinto" is famous. === Mizuko and Sorei syncretism === The Shrine has a unique dual worship of [[Sorei]] or ancestral spirits alongside [[Mizuko kuyō]]{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=239}} or cults of miscarried babies. The shrine started as a place for the Kibi clan. It has the clan's ancestors as gods. This gives the shrine a pure and protective feel. The ancestors are seen as good and helpful spirits. This is how the shrine connects with [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] means the souls of babies who died early or were not born.{{Rp|page=239}} The shrine places the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] shrine next to the ancestor shrine. It also uses running water. This setup has several meanings:{{Rp|page=239}} # The water purifies the souls of [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] is linked to water.{{Rp|page=239}} # Being near the ancestor shrine suggests these souls become kind and protective spirits.{{Rp|page=239}} # As protective spirits, the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] guard those who remember them.{{Rp|page=239}} This way, the Kibitsu Shrine uses its ties to the Kibi clan. It creates a respectful place for [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. It links them to the shrine's ancestral and protective gods.{{Rp|page=239}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Kibitsu Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]]'''|吉備津彦命|}}, the son of [[Emperor Kōrei]] and conqueror of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]] and founder of the [[Kibi clan]] * {{nihongo|'''Mitomowake-no-mikoto'''| 御友別命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Nakatsuhiko-no-mikoto| 仲彦命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Chichihaya-hime-no-mikoto'''|千々速比売命|}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Yamato-totohimomoso-hime-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日百襲姫命 |}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosasukatawake-no-mikoto'''| 日子刺肩別命|}}, elder brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosashikatawake-no-mikoto'''| 彦刺肩別命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hiko same ma no mikoto'''|彦寤間命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Wakahiko Takekibitsu Hikono-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日稚屋媛命|}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko ==History== The origins of Kibitsu Jinja are uncertain. According to the shrine's legend, it is located at the site of Kibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto's residence, where he died at the age of 281, and was buried on the summit of the mountain. Afterwards, the residence was turned into a shrine, possibly by his fifth generation descendent Narumi Kaya, or by [[Emperor Nintoku]], who visited [[Kibi Province]] where he built several shrines to commemorate Kibitsuhiko. However, the shrine does not appear in any historical documentation until the late [[Heian period]], until entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'' dated 847 and the ''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' dated 852. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'' it was given the rank of {{nihongo|''Myojin Taisha''|名神大社||}} and the rank of ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of the province. From the [[Kamakura period|Kamakura]] through the [[Sengoku period]], was revered by the samurai, and there were frequent restorations of the shrine and donations of territory. {{Citation needed|date=November 2023}} During the [[Edo period]], the shrine's land became smaller. However, it still got a special land grant from the shogunate. This grant was for 160 koku of rice every year. There was a busy market near the shrine. People also visited teahouses and inns there. Inside the shrine area, there was a theater and a brothel. The shrine was a busy place along the [[San'yōdō|San’yodō]] for travellers. This continued until the [[Meiji Restoration]]..{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=282}} After the [[Meiji Restoration]] in 1871, it was listed as a {{nihongo|National Shrine, 2nd rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Chusha}}, and is 1914 was promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial Shrine, 2nd rank|官幣中社|Kampei Chusha}}.{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese}}{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} The shrine is a ten-minute walk from [[Kibitsu Station]] on the [[JR West]] [[Kibi Line]]. ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *''[[Honden]]'' and ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]]'', [[Muromachi period]], built in 1390 and relocated their present locations in 1425.The main shrine has a ''Kibitsu-zukuri'' style roof, which consists of two [[East Asian hip-and-gable roof|''Irimoya-zukuri'']] roof are lined up in front and behind. The influence of Buddhist architecture can be seen in many details of the structure.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2993 |title= 吉備津神社本殿及び拝殿|trans-title=Kibitsu {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Okayama Prefecture, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=November 2019}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Kibitsu Jinja
吉備津神社 | image = Kibitsu Jinja 10 cropped.jpg | caption = [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]] (1425), a [[National Treasures of Japan|National Treasure]] {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|14.4|N|133|51|2.2|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title, inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = Kibitsu Jinja | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 931 Kibitsu, Kita-ku, Okayama-shi, Okayama-ken 701-1341 | website = {{official|1=https://kibitujinja.com}} | architecture_style = | festivals = Second Sunday in May and October 15th each year | leadership = | footnotes = }} {{nihongo|'''Kibitsu Jinja'''|吉備津神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in the Kibitsu neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' (first shrine) of former [[Bitchū Province]]. The shrine’s main festivals are held on the second Sunday in May and October 15th each year.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} ==Overview== The Kibitsu Jinja is located in the western part of Okayama city, facing north at the northwestern foot of Mount Kibi-Nakayama (elevation 175 meters) on the border between former [[Bizen Province]] and Bitchū Province. The mountain has been worshipped as a [[sacred mountain]] from ancient times, and both the Kibitsu Jinja and [[Kibitsuhiko Shrine|Kibitsuhiko Jinja]] are located at its northeastern foot. Kibitsu Jinja was originally the general guardian of [[Kibi Province]], but due to the division of Kibi Province into three provinces, it became the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of Bitchū, and ''[[bunrei]]'' from this shrine created the ''ichinomiya'' of Bizen Province (Kibitsuhiko Jinja) and [[Bingo Province]] (Kibitsu Shrine). The [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]], which was re-built by [[Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]], is a [[National Treasures of Japan|National Treasure]] and the sole exemplar of the ''[[kibitsu-zukuri]]'' style of [[Japanese architecture|architecture]], although the [[Dō (architecture)|Soshidō]] of [[Hokekyō-ji (Ichikawa)|Hokekyō-ji]] is now believed to have been modeled thereon.{{cite web |url=http://www.aisf.or.jp/~jaanus/deta/k/kibitsuzukuri.htm |title=Kibitsu-zukuri |publisher=[[Japanese Architecture and Art Net Users System]] |access-date=4 May 2011}}{{cite book |title=Architectural Preservation in Japan |author=Larsen, Knut Einar |publisher=[[ICOMOS]] International Wood Committee |year=1994 |pages=121–5 |isbn=82-519-1432-9}} In addition, the three shrine buildings are designated as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]], and a special Shinto ritual "Narukama Shinto" is famous. === Mizuko and Sorei syncretism === The Shrine has a unique dual worship of [[Sorei]] or ancestral spirits alongside [[Mizuko kuyō]]{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=239}} or cults of miscarried babies. The shrine started as a place for the Kibi clan. It has the clan's ancestors as gods. This gives the shrine a pure and protective feel. The ancestors are seen as good and helpful spirits. This is how the shrine connects with [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] means the souls of babies who died early or were not born.{{Rp|page=239}} The shrine places the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] shrine next to the ancestor shrine. It also uses running water. This setup has several meanings:{{Rp|page=239}} # The water purifies the souls of [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] is linked to water.{{Rp|page=239}} # Being near the ancestor shrine suggests these souls become kind and protective spirits.{{Rp|page=239}} # As protective spirits, the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] guard those who remember them.{{Rp|page=239}} This way, the Kibitsu Shrine uses its ties to the Kibi clan. It creates a respectful place for [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. It links them to the shrine's ancestral and protective gods.{{Rp|page=239}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Kibitsu Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]]'''|吉備津彦命|}}, the son of [[Emperor Kōrei]] and conqueror of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]] and founder of the [[Kibi clan]] * {{nihongo|'''Mitomowake-no-mikoto'''| 御友別命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Nakatsuhiko-no-mikoto| 仲彦命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Chichihaya-hime-no-mikoto'''|千々速比売命|}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Yamato-totohimomoso-hime-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日百襲姫命 |}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosasukatawake-no-mikoto'''| 日子刺肩別命|}}, elder brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosashikatawake-no-mikoto'''| 彦刺肩別命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hiko same ma no mikoto'''|彦寤間命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Wakahiko Takekibitsu Hikono-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日稚屋媛命|}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko ==History== The origins of Kibitsu Jinja are uncertain. According to the shrine's legend, it is located at the site of Kibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto's residence, where he died at the age of 281, and was buried on the summit of the mountain. Afterwards, the residence was turned into a shrine, possibly by his fifth generation descendent Narumi Kaya, or by [[Emperor Nintoku]], who visited [[Kibi Province]] where he built several shrines to commemorate Kibitsuhiko. However, the shrine does not appear in any historical documentation until the late [[Heian period]], until entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'' dated 847 and the ''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' dated 852. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'' it was given the rank of {{nihongo|''Myojin Taisha''|名神大社||}} and the rank of ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of the province. From the [[Kamakura period|Kamakura]] through the [[Sengoku period]], was revered by the samurai, and there were frequent restorations of the shrine and donations of territory. {{Citation needed|date=November 2023}} During the [[Edo period]], the shrine's land became smaller. However, it still got a special land grant from the shogunate. This grant was for 160 koku of rice every year. There was a busy market near the shrine. People also visited teahouses and inns there. Inside the shrine area, there was a theater and a brothel. The shrine was a busy place along the [[San'yōdō|San’yodō]] for travellers. The influence of Buddhist architecture can be seen in many details of the structure.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2993 |title= 吉備津神社本殿及び拝殿|trans-title=Kibitsu {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Okayama Prefecture, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=November 2019}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Kibitsu Jinja
吉備津神社 | image = Kibitsu Jinja 10 cropped.jpg | caption = [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]] (1425), a [[National Treasures of Japan|National Treasure]] {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|14.4|N|133|51|2.2|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title, inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = Kibitsu Jinja | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 931 Kibitsu, Kita-ku, Okayama-shi, Okayama-ken 701-1341 | website = {{official|1=https://kibitujinja.com}} | architecture_style = | festivals = Second Sunday in May and October 15th each year | leadership = | footnotes = }} {{nihongo|'''Kibitsu Jinja'''|吉備津神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in the Kibitsu neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' (first shrine) of former [[Bitchū Province]]. The shrine’s main festivals are held on the second Sunday in May and October 15th each year.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} ==Overview== The Kibitsu Jinja is located in the western part of Okayama city, facing north at the northwestern foot of Mount Kibi-Nakayama (elevation 175 meters) on the border between former [[Bizen Province]] and Bitchū Province. The mountain has been worshipped as a [[sacred mountain]] from ancient times, and both the Kibitsu Jinja and [[Kibitsuhiko Shrine|Kibitsuhiko Jinja]] are located at its northeastern foot. Kibitsu Jinja was originally the general guardian of [[Kibi Province]], but due to the division of Kibi Province into three provinces, it became the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of Bitchū, and ''[[bunrei]]'' from this shrine created the ''ichinomiya'' of Bizen Province (Kibitsuhiko Jinja) and [[Bingo Province]] (Kibitsu Shrine). The [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]], which was re-built by [[Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]], is a [[National Treasures of Japan|National Treasure]] and the sole exemplar of the ''[[kibitsu-zukuri]]'' style of [[Japanese architecture|architecture]], although the [[Dō (architecture)|Soshidō]] of [[Hokekyō-ji (Ichikawa)|Hokekyō-ji]] is now believed to have been modeled thereon.{{cite web |url=http://www.aisf.or.jp/~jaanus/deta/k/kibitsuzukuri.htm |title=Kibitsu-zukuri |publisher=[[Japanese Architecture and Art Net Users System]] |access-date=4 May 2011}}{{cite book |title=Architectural Preservation in Japan |author=Larsen, Knut Einar |publisher=[[ICOMOS]] International Wood Committee |year=1994 |pages=121–5 |isbn=82-519-1432-9}} In addition, the three shrine buildings are designated as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]], and a special Shinto ritual "Narukama Shinto" is famous. === Mizuko and Sorei syncretism === The Shrine has a unique dual worship of [[Sorei]] or ancestral spirits alongside [[Mizuko kuyō]]{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=239}} or cults of miscarried babies. The shrine started as a place for the Kibi clan. It has the clan's ancestors as gods. This gives the shrine a pure and protective feel. The ancestors are seen as good and helpful spirits. This is how the shrine connects with [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] means the souls of babies who died early or were not born.{{Rp|page=239}} The shrine places the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] shrine next to the ancestor shrine. It also uses running water. This setup has several meanings:{{Rp|page=239}} # The water purifies the souls of [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] is linked to water.{{Rp|page=239}} # Being near the ancestor shrine suggests these souls become kind and protective spirits.{{Rp|page=239}} # As protective spirits, the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] guard those who remember them.{{Rp|page=239}} This way, the Kibitsu Shrine uses its ties to the Kibi clan. It creates a respectful place for [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. It links them to the shrine's ancestral and protective gods.{{Rp|page=239}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Kibitsu Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]]'''|吉備津彦命|}}, the son of [[Emperor Kōrei]] and conqueror of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]] and founder of the [[Kibi clan]] * {{nihongo|'''Mitomowake-no-mikoto'''| 御友別命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Nakatsuhiko-no-mikoto| 仲彦命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Chichihaya-hime-no-mikoto'''|千々速比売命|}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Yamato-totohimomoso-hime-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日百襲姫命 |}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosasukatawake-no-mikoto'''| 日子刺肩別命|}}, elder brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosashikatawake-no-mikoto'''| 彦刺肩別命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hiko same ma no mikoto'''|彦寤間命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Wakahiko Takekibitsu Hikono-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日稚屋媛命|}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko ==History== The origins of Kibitsu Jinja are uncertain. According to the shrine's legend, it is located at the site of Kibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto's residence, where he died at the age of 281, and was buried on the summit of the mountain. Afterwards, the residence was turned into a shrine, possibly by his fifth generation descendent Narumi Kaya, or by [[Emperor Nintoku]], who visited [[Kibi Province]] where he built several shrines to commemorate Kibitsuhiko. However, the shrine does not appear in any historical documentation until the late [[Heian period]], until entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'' dated 847 and the ''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' dated 852. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'' it was given the rank of {{nihongo|''Myojin Taisha''|名神大社||}} and the rank of ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of the province. From the [[Kamakura period|Kamakura]] through the [[Sengoku period]], was revered by the samurai, and there were frequent restorations of the shrine and donations of territory. {{Citation needed|date=November 2023}} During the [[Edo period]], the shrine's land became smaller. However, it still got a special land grant from the shogunate. This grant was for 160 koku of rice every year. There was a busy market near the shrine. People also visited teahouses and inns there. Inside the shrine area, there was a theater and a brothel. The shrine was a busy place along the [[San'yōdō|San’yodō]] for travellers. This continued until the [[Meiji Restoration]]..{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=282}} After the [[Meiji Restoration]] in 1871, it was listed as a {{nihongo|National Shrine, 2nd rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Chusha}}, and is 1914 was promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial Shrine, 2nd rank|官幣中社|Kampei Chusha}}.{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese}}{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} The shrine is a ten-minute walk from [[Kibitsu Station]] on the [[JR West]] [[Kibi Line]]. ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *''[[Honden]]'' and ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]]'', [[Muromachi period]], built in 1390 and relocated their present locations in 1425.The main shrine has a ''Kibitsu-zukuri'' style roof, which consists of two [[East Asian hip-and-gable roof|''Irimoya-zukuri'']] roof are lined up in front and behind. {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Okayama Prefecture, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=November 2019}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Kibitsu Jinja
吉備津神社 | image = Kibitsu Jinja 10 cropped.jpg | caption = [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]] (1425), a [[National Treasures of Japan|National Treasure]] {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|14.4|N|133|51|2.2|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title, inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = Kibitsu Jinja | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 931 Kibitsu, Kita-ku, Okayama-shi, Okayama-ken 701-1341 | website = {{official|1=https://kibitujinja.com}} | architecture_style = | festivals = Second Sunday in May and October 15th each year | leadership = | footnotes = }} {{nihongo|'''Kibitsu Jinja'''|吉備津神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in the Kibitsu neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' (first shrine) of former [[Bitchū Province]]. The shrine’s main festivals are held on the second Sunday in May and October 15th each year.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} ==Overview== The Kibitsu Jinja is located in the western part of Okayama city, facing north at the northwestern foot of Mount Kibi-Nakayama (elevation 175 meters) on the border between former [[Bizen Province]] and Bitchū Province. The mountain has been worshipped as a [[sacred mountain]] from ancient times, and both the Kibitsu Jinja and [[Kibitsuhiko Shrine|Kibitsuhiko Jinja]] are located at its northeastern foot. Kibitsu Jinja was originally the general guardian of [[Kibi Province]], but due to the division of Kibi Province into three provinces, it became the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of Bitchū, and ''[[bunrei]]'' from this shrine created the ''ichinomiya'' of Bizen Province (Kibitsuhiko Jinja) and [[Bingo Province]] (Kibitsu Shrine). The [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]], which was re-built by [[Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]], is a [[National Treasures of Japan|National Treasure]] and the sole exemplar of the ''[[kibitsu-zukuri]]'' style of [[Japanese architecture|architecture]], although the [[Dō (architecture)|Soshidō]] of [[Hokekyō-ji (Ichikawa)|Hokekyō-ji]] is now believed to have been modeled thereon.{{cite web |url=http://www.aisf.or.jp/~jaanus/deta/k/kibitsuzukuri.htm |title=Kibitsu-zukuri |publisher=[[Japanese Architecture and Art Net Users System]] |access-date=4 May 2011}}{{cite book |title=Architectural Preservation in Japan |author=Larsen, Knut Einar |publisher=[[ICOMOS]] International Wood Committee |year=1994 |pages=121–5 |isbn=82-519-1432-9}} In addition, the three shrine buildings are designated as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]], and a special Shinto ritual "Narukama Shinto" is famous. === Mizuko and Sorei syncretism === The Shrine has a unique dual worship of [[Sorei]] or ancestral spirits alongside [[Mizuko kuyō]]{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=239}} or cults of miscarried babies. The shrine started as a place for the Kibi clan. It has the clan's ancestors as gods. This gives the shrine a pure and protective feel. The ancestors are seen as good and helpful spirits. This is how the shrine connects with [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] means the souls of babies who died early or were not born.{{Rp|page=239}} The shrine places the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] shrine next to the ancestor shrine. It also uses running water. This setup has several meanings:{{Rp|page=239}} # The water purifies the souls of [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] is linked to water.{{Rp|page=239}} # Being near the ancestor shrine suggests these souls become kind and protective spirits.{{Rp|page=239}} # As protective spirits, the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] guard those who remember them.{{Rp|page=239}} This way, the Kibitsu Shrine uses its ties to the Kibi clan. It creates a respectful place for [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. It links them to the shrine's ancestral and protective gods.{{Rp|page=239}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Kibitsu Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]]'''|吉備津彦命|}}, the son of [[Emperor Kōrei]] and conqueror of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]] and founder of the [[Kibi clan]] * {{nihongo|'''Mitomowake-no-mikoto'''| 御友別命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Nakatsuhiko-no-mikoto| 仲彦命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Chichihaya-hime-no-mikoto'''|千々速比売命|}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Yamato-totohimomoso-hime-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日百襲姫命 |}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosasukatawake-no-mikoto'''| 日子刺肩別命|}}, elder brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosashikatawake-no-mikoto'''| 彦刺肩別命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hiko same ma no mikoto'''|彦寤間命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Wakahiko Takekibitsu Hikono-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日稚屋媛命|}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko ==History== The origins of Kibitsu Jinja are uncertain. According to the shrine's legend, it is located at the site of Kibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto's residence, where he died at the age of 281, and was buried on the summit of the mountain. Afterwards, the residence was turned into a shrine, possibly by his fifth generation descendent Narumi Kaya, or by [[Emperor Nintoku]], who visited [[Kibi Province]] where he built several shrines to commemorate Kibitsuhiko. However, the shrine does not appear in any historical documentation until the late [[Heian period]], until entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'' dated 847 and the ''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' dated 852. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'' it was given the rank of {{nihongo|''Myojin Taisha''|名神大社||}} and the rank of ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of the province. From the [[Kamakura period|Kamakura]] through the [[Sengoku period]], was revered by the samurai, and there were frequent restorations of the shrine and donations of territory. {{Citation needed|date=November 2023}} During the [[Edo period]], the shrine's land became smaller. However, it still got a special land grant from the shogunate. This grant was for 160 koku of rice every year. There was a busy market near the shrine. People also visited teahouses and inns there. Inside the shrine area, there was a theater and a brothel. The shrine was a busy place along the [[San'yōdō|San’yodō]] for travellers. This continued until the [[Meiji Restoration]]..{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=282}} After the [[Meiji Restoration]] in 1871, it was listed as a {{nihongo|National Shrine, 2nd rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Chusha}}, and is 1914 was promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial Shrine, 2nd rank|官幣中社|Kampei Chusha}}.{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese}}{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} The shrine is a ten-minute walk from [[Kibitsu Station]] on the [[JR West]] [[Kibi Line]]. ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *''[[Honden]]'' and ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]]'', [[Muromachi period]], built in 1390 and relocated their present locations in 1425.The main shrine has a ''Kibitsu-zukuri'' style roof, which consists of two [[East Asian hip-and-gable roof|''Irimoya-zukuri'']] roof are lined up in front and behind. The influence of Buddhist architecture can be seen in many details of the structure.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2993 |title= 吉備津神社本殿及び拝殿|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine main hall and worship hall|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} ===Important Cultural Properties=== *{{nihongo|'''South Zuishinmon'''|南随神門||}}, [[Muromachi period]], built in 1357.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2994 |title=吉備津神社南随神門|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine South The shrine’s main festivals are held on the second Sunday in May and October 15th each year.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} ==Overview== The Kibitsu Jinja is located in the western part of Okayama city, facing north at the northwestern foot of Mount Kibi-Nakayama (elevation 175 meters) on the border between former [[Bizen Province]] and Bitchū Province. Kibitsu Jinja was originally the general guardian of [[Kibi Province]], but due to the division of Kibi Province into three provinces, it became the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of Bitchū, and ''[[bunrei]]'' from this shrine created the ''ichinomiya'' of Bizen Province (Kibitsuhiko Jinja) and [[Bingo Province]] (Kibitsu Shrine). The [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]], which was re-built by [[Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]], is a [[National Treasures of Japan|National Treasure]] and the sole exemplar of the ''[[kibitsu-zukuri]]'' style of [[Japanese architecture|architecture]], although the [[Dō (architecture)|Soshidō]] of [[Hokekyō-ji (Ichikawa)|Hokekyō-ji]] is now believed to have been modeled thereon.{{cite web |url=http://www.aisf.or.jp/~jaanus/deta/k/kibitsuzukuri.htm |title=Kibitsu-zukuri |publisher=[[Japanese Architecture and Art Net Users System]] |access-date=4 May 2011}}{{cite book |title=Architectural Preservation in Japan |author=Larsen, Knut Einar |publisher=[[ICOMOS]] International Wood Committee |year=1994 |pages=121–5 |isbn=82-519-1432-9}} In addition, the three shrine buildings are designated as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]], and a special Shinto ritual "Narukama Shinto" is famous. === Mizuko and Sorei syncretism === The Shrine has a unique dual worship of [[Sorei]] or ancestral spirits alongside [[Mizuko kuyō]]{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=239}} or cults of miscarried babies. The shrine started as a place for the Kibi clan. It has the clan's ancestors as gods. This gives the shrine a pure and protective feel. The ancestors are seen as good and helpful spirits. This is how the shrine connects with [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] means the souls of babies who died early or were not born.{{Rp|page=239}} The shrine places the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] shrine next to the ancestor shrine. It also uses running water. This setup has several meanings:{{Rp|page=239}} # The water purifies the souls of [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] is linked to water.{{Rp|page=239}} # Being near the ancestor shrine suggests these souls become kind and protective spirits.{{Rp|page=239}} # As protective spirits, the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] guard those who remember them.{{Rp|page=239}} This way, the Kibitsu Shrine uses its ties to the Kibi clan. It creates a respectful place for [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. It links them to the shrine's ancestral and protective gods.{{Rp|page=239}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Kibitsu Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]]'''|吉備津彦命|}}, the son of [[Emperor Kōrei]] and conqueror of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]] and founder of the [[Kibi clan]] * {{nihongo|'''Mitomowake-no-mikoto'''| 御友別命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Nakatsuhiko-no-mikoto| 仲彦命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Chichihaya-hime-no-mikoto'''|千々速比売命|}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Yamato-totohimomoso-hime-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日百襲姫命 |}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosasukatawake-no-mikoto'''| 日子刺肩別命|}}, elder brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosashikatawake-no-mikoto'''| 彦刺肩別命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hiko same ma no mikoto'''|彦寤間命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Wakahiko Takekibitsu Hikono-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日稚屋媛命|}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko ==History== The origins of Kibitsu Jinja are uncertain. According to the shrine's legend, it is located at the site of Kibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto's residence, where he died at the age of 281, and was buried on the summit of the mountain. Afterwards, the residence was turned into a shrine, possibly by his fifth generation descendent Narumi Kaya, or by [[Emperor Nintoku]], who visited [[Kibi Province]] where he built several shrines to commemorate Kibitsuhiko. However, the shrine does not appear in any historical documentation until the late [[Heian period]], until entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'' dated 847 and the ''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' dated 852. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'' it was given the rank of {{nihongo|''Myojin Taisha''|名神大社||}} and the rank of ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of the province. From the [[Kamakura period|Kamakura]] through the [[Sengoku period]], was revered by the samurai, and there were frequent restorations of the shrine and donations of territory. {{Citation needed|date=November 2023}} During the [[Edo period]], the shrine's land became smaller. However, it still got a special land grant from the shogunate. This grant was for 160 koku of rice every year. There was a busy market near the shrine. People also visited teahouses and inns there. Inside the shrine area, there was a theater and a brothel. The shrine was a busy place along the [[San'yōdō|San’yodō]] for travellers. This continued until the [[Meiji Restoration]]..{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=282}} After the [[Meiji Restoration]] in 1871, it was listed as a {{nihongo|National Shrine, 2nd rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Chusha}}, and is 1914 was promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial Shrine, 2nd rank|官幣中社|Kampei Chusha}}.{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese}}{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} The shrine is a ten-minute walk from [[Kibitsu Station]] on the [[JR West]] [[Kibi Line]]. ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *''[[Honden]]'' and ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]]'', [[Muromachi period]], built in 1390 and relocated their present locations in 1425.The main shrine has a ''Kibitsu-zukuri'' style roof, which consists of two [[East Asian hip-and-gable roof|''Irimoya-zukuri'']] roof are lined up in front and behind. The influence of Buddhist architecture can be seen in many details of the structure.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2993 |title= 吉備津神社本殿及び拝殿|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine main hall and worship hall|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} ===Important Cultural Properties=== *{{nihongo|'''South Zuishinmon'''|南随神門||}}, [[Muromachi period]], built in 1357.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2994 |title=吉備津神社南随神門|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine South Zuijinmon|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} *{{nihongo|'''North Zuishinmon'''|北随神門||}}, [[Sengoku period]], built in 1543.{{cite web |access-date=August 20, 2020}} *{{nihongo|'''Okama-den'''|御釜殿||}}, [[Edo period]], built in 1612.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2996 |title= Period|Kamakura]] to [[Nanboku-cho period]], Located to the east and west of the Honden.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/10545 |title= 木造獅子狛犬|trans-title=Mokuzō {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Okayama Prefecture, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=November 2019}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Kibitsu Jinja
吉備津神社 | image = Kibitsu Jinja 10 cropped.jpg | caption = [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]] (1425), a [[National Treasures of Japan|National Treasure]] {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|14.4|N|133|51|2.2|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title, inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = Kibitsu Jinja | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 931 Kibitsu, Kita-ku, Okayama-shi, Okayama-ken 701-1341 | website = {{official|1=https://kibitujinja.com}} | architecture_style = | festivals = Second Sunday in May and October 15th each year | leadership = | footnotes = }} {{nihongo|'''Kibitsu Jinja'''|吉備津神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in the Kibitsu neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' (first shrine) of former [[Bitchū Province]]. The shrine’s main festivals are held on the second Sunday in May and October 15th each year.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} ==Overview== The Kibitsu Jinja is located in the western part of Okayama city, facing north at the northwestern foot of Mount Kibi-Nakayama (elevation 175 meters) on the border between former [[Bizen Province]] and Bitchū Province. The mountain has been worshipped as a [[sacred mountain]] from ancient times, and both the Kibitsu Jinja and [[Kibitsuhiko Shrine|Kibitsuhiko Jinja]] are located at its northeastern foot. Kibitsu Jinja was originally the general guardian of [[Kibi Province]], but due to the division of Kibi Province into three provinces, it became the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of Bitchū, and ''[[bunrei]]'' from this shrine created the ''ichinomiya'' of Bizen Province (Kibitsuhiko Jinja) and [[Bingo Province]] (Kibitsu Shrine). The [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]], which was re-built by [[Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]], is a [[National Treasures of Japan|National Treasure]] and the sole exemplar of the ''[[kibitsu-zukuri]]'' style of [[Japanese architecture|architecture]], although the [[Dō (architecture)|Soshidō]] of [[Hokekyō-ji (Ichikawa)|Hokekyō-ji]] is now believed to have been modeled thereon.{{cite web |url=http://www.aisf.or.jp/~jaanus/deta/k/kibitsuzukuri.htm |title=Kibitsu-zukuri |publisher=[[Japanese Architecture and Art Net Users System]] |access-date=4 May 2011}}{{cite book |title=Architectural Preservation in Japan |author=Larsen, Knut Einar |publisher=[[ICOMOS]] International Wood Committee |year=1994 |pages=121–5 |isbn=82-519-1432-9}} In addition, the three shrine buildings are designated as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]], and a special Shinto ritual "Narukama Shinto" is famous. === Mizuko and Sorei syncretism === The Shrine has a unique dual worship of [[Sorei]] or ancestral spirits alongside [[Mizuko kuyō]]{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=239}} or cults of miscarried babies. The shrine started as a place for the Kibi clan. It has the clan's ancestors as gods. This gives the shrine a pure and protective feel. The ancestors are seen as good and helpful spirits. This is how the shrine connects with [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] means the souls of babies who died early or were not born.{{Rp|page=239}} The shrine places the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] shrine next to the ancestor shrine. It also uses running water. This setup has several meanings:{{Rp|page=239}} # The water purifies the souls of [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] is linked to water.{{Rp|page=239}} # Being near the ancestor shrine suggests these souls become kind and protective spirits.{{Rp|page=239}} # As protective spirits, the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] guard those who remember them.{{Rp|page=239}} This way, the Kibitsu Shrine uses its ties to the Kibi clan. It creates a respectful place for [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. It links them to the shrine's ancestral and protective gods.{{Rp|page=239}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Kibitsu Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]]'''|吉備津彦命|}}, the son of [[Emperor Kōrei]] and conqueror of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]] and founder of the [[Kibi clan]] * {{nihongo|'''Mitomowake-no-mikoto'''| 御友別命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Nakatsuhiko-no-mikoto| 仲彦命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Chichihaya-hime-no-mikoto'''|千々速比売命|}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Yamato-totohimomoso-hime-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日百襲姫命 |}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosasukatawake-no-mikoto'''| 日子刺肩別命|}}, elder brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosashikatawake-no-mikoto'''| 彦刺肩別命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hiko same ma no mikoto'''|彦寤間命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Wakahiko Takekibitsu Hikono-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日稚屋媛命|}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko ==History== The origins of Kibitsu Jinja are uncertain. According to the shrine's legend, it is located at the site of Kibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto's residence, where he died at the age of 281, and was buried on the summit of the mountain. Afterwards, the residence was turned into a shrine, possibly by his fifth generation descendent Narumi Kaya, or by [[Emperor Nintoku]], who visited [[Kibi Province]] where he built several shrines to commemorate Kibitsuhiko. However, the shrine does not appear in any historical documentation until the late [[Heian period]], until entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'' dated 847 and the ''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' dated 852. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'' it was given the rank of {{nihongo|''Myojin Taisha''|名神大社||}} and the rank of ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of the province. From the [[Kamakura period|Kamakura]] through the [[Sengoku period]], was revered by the samurai, and there were frequent restorations of the shrine and donations of territory. {{Citation needed|date=November 2023}} During the [[Edo period]], the shrine's land became smaller. However, it still got a special land grant from the shogunate. This grant was for 160 koku of rice every year. There was a busy market near the shrine. People also visited teahouses and inns there. Inside the shrine area, there was a theater and a brothel. The shrine was a busy place along the [[San'yōdō|San’yodō]] for travellers. This continued until the [[Meiji Restoration]]..{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=282}} After the [[Meiji Restoration]] in 1871, it was listed as a {{nihongo|National Shrine, 2nd rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Chusha}}, and is 1914 was promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial Shrine, 2nd rank|官幣中社|Kampei Chusha}}.{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese}}{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} The shrine is a ten-minute walk from [[Kibitsu Station]] on the [[JR West]] [[Kibi Line]]. ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *''[[Honden]]'' and ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]]'', [[Muromachi period]], built in 1390 and relocated their present locations in 1425.The main shrine has a ''Kibitsu-zukuri'' style roof, which consists of two [[East Asian hip-and-gable roof|''Irimoya-zukuri'']] roof are lined up in front and behind. The influence of Buddhist architecture can be seen in many details of the structure.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2993 |title= 吉備津神社本殿及び拝殿|trans-title=Kibitsu （わちがい もん）]] [[File:吉備の中山 (吉備津神社から).JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|[[神体山]]とする吉備の中山}}{{small|右端は参道の松並木。}}]] [[File:Kibitsu Jinja -02.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|入り口の[[注連縄]]}}]] '''吉備津神社'''（きびつじんじゃ）は、[[岡山県]][[岡山市]][[北区 (岡山市)|北区]][[吉備津]]にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]（[[名神大社]]）、[[備中国]][[一宮]]。[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[官幣中社]]で、現在は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]。 「吉備津彦神社（きびつひこじんじゃ）」とも称したが、現在は「吉備津神社」が正式名である現在、備中・備後一宮は「吉備津神社」を名乗るが、備前一宮のみ「吉備津彦神社」を名乗る。。 == 概要 == 岡山市西部、[[備前国]]と[[備中国]]の境の[[吉備中山]]（標高175メートル）の北西麓に北面して鎮座する。吉備中山は古来[[神体山]]とされ、北東麓には備前国一宮・[[吉備津彦神社]]が鎮座する。当社と吉備津彦神社とも、主祭神に、当地を治めたとされる[[吉備津彦命|大吉備津彦命]]を祀り、命の一族を配祀する。 本来は[[吉備国]]の総鎮守であったが、吉備国の三国への分割により備中国の一宮とされ、分霊が備前国・[[備後国]]の一宮（備前：[[吉備津彦神社]]、備後：[[吉備津神社 (福山市)|吉備津神社]]）となったとされる。この事から備中の吉備津神社は「吉備総鎮守」「三備一宮」を名乗る{{Cite book |和書 |title=まいられぇ岡山 2016年版|publisher=[[山陽新聞社]] |year=2016 |page=54}}なお備前の吉備津彦神社側では、分霊による創建の伝承はない。。 [[足利義満]]造営とされる本殿は全国唯一の[[比翼入母屋造]]（吉備津造）で、拝殿とともに[[国宝]]に指定。また社殿3棟が国の[[重要文化財]]に指定されるほか、特殊神事の[[鳴釜神事]]が有名である。 当地出身の政治家[[犬養毅]]は、犬養家遠祖の犬飼健命が大吉備津彦命の随神であるとして、吉備津神社を崇敬したという{{Cite web|和書|url=https://okayama-kanko.net/sightseeing/_cms/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/85ba4c00217acc9f333e2c3496cdce52.pdf|title=吉備路周遊マップ|publisher=公益社団法人おかやま観光コンベンション協会|date=|accessdate=2024-11-10|page=9-10}}。神池の畔に犬養毅の銅像が建てられ、吉備津神社の社号標も同人の揮毫によるものである。 == 祭神 == 祭神は次の9柱。 ; 主祭神 :* [[吉備津彦命|大吉備津彦命]]（おおきびつひこのみこと） :*: 第7代[[孝霊天皇]]の第三皇子で、元の名を「彦五十狭芹彦命（ひこいせさりひこのみこと、五十狭芹彦命）」。[[崇神天皇]]10年、[[四道将軍]]の1人として山陽道に派遣され、弟の若日子建吉備津彦命と吉備を平定した。その子孫が吉備の[[国造]]となり、古代豪族の[[吉備氏|吉備臣]]になったとされる。 ; 相殿神 :* 百田弓矢比売命（ももたゆみやひめのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の后。 :* [[御友別命]]（みともわけのみことのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の子孫。 :* 仲彦命（なかつひこのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の子孫。 :* [[千千速比売命|千々速比売命]]（ちちはやひめのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の姉。 :* [[倭迹迹日百襲姫命]]（やまとととひももそひめのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の姉。 :* 日子刺肩別命（ひこさすかたわけのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の兄。 :* [[倭迹迹稚屋姫命|倭迹迹日稚屋媛命]]（やまとととひわかやひめのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の妹。 :* [[彦狭島命|彦寤間命]]（ひこさめまのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の弟。 :* [[稚武彦命|若日子建吉備津日子命]]（わかひこたけきびつひこのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の弟。 古くは「吉備津五所大明神」として、正宮と他の4社の5社で1つの神社を成した（他4社の祭神は後述の「[[吉備津神社#摂末社|摂末社]]」項参照）。

{{clear}} == 歴史 == === 創建 === 社伝によれば、祭神の大吉備津彦命は吉備中山の麓の茅葺宮に住み、281歳で亡くなって山頂に葬られた。5代目の子孫の加夜臣奈留美命が茅葺宮に社殿を造営し、命を祀ったのが創建とする説もある。また、吉備国に行幸した[[仁徳天皇]]が、大吉備津彦命の業績を称えて5つの社殿と72の末社を創建したという説もある。 === 概史 === [[朝廷 (日本)|朝廷]]からの篤い崇敬を受け、国史では[[承和 (日本)|承和]]14年（[[847年]]）に従四位下の[[神階]]を受けた記載が最初で、翌年には従四位上に進んだ。[[仁寿]]2年（[[852年]]）には神階が[[品位 (位階)|品位]]（ほんい）に変わって四品（しほん）が授けられ、[[10世紀]]には一品（いっぽん）まで昇叙された。 [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）成立の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]では[[備中国]][[賀夜郡]]に「吉備津彦神社 名神大」と記載され、[[名神大社]]に列している[[皇學館大学]]出版部『式内社調査報告 第二十二巻 山陽道』。。 中世には武家の崇敬を受け、たびたび社殿の修復や社領の寄進があった。[[江戸]]中期には[[三重塔]]を破却し神仏分離を行った。 [[明治維新]]後、[[明治]]4年（[[1871年]]）に[[近代社格制度]]において[[国幣中社]]に列し、公称を現在の「吉備津神社」に定めた。[[大正]]3年（[[1914年]]）には[[官幣中社]]に昇格した。 === 神階 === * 六国史時代における神階奉叙の記録 ** [[承和 (日本)|承和]]14年（[[847年]]）10月22日、無位から従四位下 （『[[続日本後紀]]』） - 表記は「吉備津彦命神」。 ** [[嘉祥]]元年（[[848年]]）2月21日、従四位上 （『続日本後紀』） - 表記は「吉備津彦命神」。 ** [[仁寿]]2年（[[852年]]）2月20日、四品、官社に列す （『[[日本文徳天皇実録]]』） - 表記は「吉備津彦命神」。 ** 仁寿2年（852年）8月27日時点、四品 （『日本文徳天皇実録』） - 表記は「吉備津彦命神」。 ** [[天安 (日本)|天安]]元年（[[857年]]）6月3日、四品から三品 （『日本文徳天皇実録』） - 表記は「吉備津彦命神」。 ** [[天安 (日本)|天安]]3年（[[859年]]）1月27日、三品から二品 （『[[日本三代実録]]』） - 表記は「吉備都彦命」。 * 六国史以後 ** [[天慶]]3年（[[940年]]）、一品 == 境内 == === 本殿および拝殿 === [[File:Kibitsu Jinja -01.jpg|thumb|400px|right|{{center|本殿と拝殿（国宝）}}]] 現存する本殿・拝殿は、[[室町時代]]の[[明徳]]元年（[[1390年]]）、[[後光厳天皇]]の命を受けた[[室町幕府]]3代将軍の[[足利義満]]が造営を開始し、[[応永]]32年（1425年）に遷座した[http://www.kibitujinja.com/about/honden.html 神社公式サイト]、[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=4 「おかやまの文化財」]（岡山県サイト）、[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/195650 文化遺産オンライン]などは本殿建立年代を応永32年（1425年）としている。『週刊朝日百科 日本の国宝』29号（朝日新聞社、1997）は、本殿は応永12年（1405年）に完成し、応永32年に屋根の仮葺きを檜皮葺きに改めて正式に遷宮したとする。。比翼入母屋造の本殿の手前に切妻造、平入りの拝殿が接続する。比翼入母屋造とは、[[入母屋造]]の屋根を前後に2つ並べた屋根形式で、「吉備津造」ともいう。 本殿の大きさは、[[出雲大社]]本殿、[[八坂神社]]本殿に匹敵するもので、随所に仏教建築の影響がみられる。地面より一段高く、漆喰塗の土壇（亀腹）の上に建ち、平面は桁行正面五間、背面七間、梁間八間で、屋根は[[檜皮葺]]とする。内部は中央に閉鎖的な内々陣とその手前の内陣があり、その周囲を一段低い中陣とし、中陣の手前はさらに一段低い朱の壇（あけのだん）とし、これらの周囲にさらに低い外陣が一周する。このように、外側から内側へ向けて徐々に床高を高くする特異な構造である。壁面上半には神社には珍しい連子窓をめぐらす。挿肘木、皿斗、虹梁の形状など、神社本殿に[[大仏様]]（だいぶつよう）を応用した唯一の例とされる。 拝殿は本殿と同時に造営され、桁行（側面）三間、梁間（正面）一間妻入りで、正面は切妻造、背面は本殿に接続。正面と側面には裳階（もこし）を設ける。屋根は本殿と同じく檜皮葺だが、裳階は本瓦葺きとする。これら本殿・拝殿は、合わせて1棟として[[国宝]]に指定されている『週刊朝日百科 日本の国宝』29号、朝日新聞社、1997、pp.'''2''' - 281 - '''2''' - 283。 === その他の社殿 === * 御釜殿 *: [[江戸時代]]、[[慶長]]11年（[[1606年]]）の鉱山師・安原知種による再建。単層入母屋造の平入で、本瓦葺。南北に伸びた長方形で、北二間に釜を置く。金曜日を除く毎日、特殊神事の「[[鳴釜神事]]」が行われる。国の重要文化財に指定されている。 * 回廊 *: [[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]、[[天正]]年間（[[1573年]] - [[1591年]]）の造営とされる。総延長398メートル。岡山県指定文化財に指定されている。 * 北随神門 *: 室町時代、[[天文 (元号)|天文]]11年（[[1542年]]）の再建。単層[[入母屋造]]檜皮葺。神社正面からの参道途中に建てられている。国の重要文化財に指定されている。 * 南随神門 *: [[南北朝時代 (日本)|南北朝時代]]、[[延文]]2年（[[1357年]]）の再建。吉備津神社では最古。単層入母屋造本瓦葺。本宮社への回廊途中に建てられている。国の重要文化財に指定されている。 File:吉備津神社 御釜殿.JPG|御釜殿（国の重要文化財） File:Kibitsu Jinja Corridor 03.JPG|回廊 File:吉備津神社 北随神門.JPG|北随神門（国の重要文化財） File:Kibitujinja5024.JPG|参道と二の鳥居 File:吉備津神社 一の鳥居.JPG|一の鳥居 == 摂末社 == [[File:本宮社 (吉備津神社境内社).JPG|right|thumb|200px|{{center|本宮社}}]] 古くは5つの社殿と72の末社があったとされる。5つの社殿（本社正宮・本宮社・新宮社・内宮社・岩山宮）を「吉備津五所大明神」と総称した『岡山県の地名』吉備津彦神社項。。現在、新宮社と内宮社は本宮社に合祀されている。 * 本宮社 - [http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=518 木造獅子狛犬]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 === 重要無形民俗文化財（国指定） === * [[備中神楽]] *: 備中地方各地で奉納される神楽で、吉備津神社では毎月10日の[[えびす祭]]で演じられる。保護団体は備中神楽保存会。昭和54年2月3日指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|302|120|備中神楽}}
[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=319 備中神楽]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 === 岡山県指定文化財 === * 重要文化財（有形文化財） ** 回廊（建造物） - 戦国時代、天正年間（1573-1591年）の造営。昭和51年3月27日指定[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=169 吉備津神社回廊]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 ** 大太刀 銘 備州長船秀幸（工芸品） - 室町時代、長禄3年（1459年）の作。岡山県立博物館に寄託。昭和57年4月9日指定[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=700 大太刀　銘備州長船秀幸]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。刃長127.2cm、反り3.9cm。鎬造り、庵棟。秀幸は、小反り派と呼ばれる[[長船派]]傍流の刀工の中でも代表的な人物。 ** 大太刀 法光（工芸品） - 室町時代、文安3年（1446年）の作。[[岡山県立博物館]]に寄託。平成6年4月5日指定[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=701 大太刀　法光]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。全長377.3cm、刃長226.7cm、反り5cm、重量13㎏。鎬造り、丸棟。古刀期では国内最大の日本刀。奉納刀で使用した形跡は無いが、刃全体に焼入れを施し、[[茎 (刀)|茎]]が長く、3つの目釘孔が均等に空いており、実戦を意識して制作されたことがわかる。 ** 行道面（工芸品） - 岡山県立博物館に寄託。昭和34年3月27日指定[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=699 行道面]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 ** 高麗版一切経（書跡・典籍） - 朝鮮の高麗時代の経典。昭和34年3月27日指定[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=594 高麗版一切経]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 ** 紙本墨書連歌（書跡・典籍） - 応永8年（1401年）に吉備津神社で行われた法楽連歌の発句を集めたもの。昭和34年3月27日指定[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=764 本墨書連歌]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 * 無形民俗文化財 ** 宮内踊 - 門前町の宮内地区で[[7月31日]]に行われる。昭和34年3月27日指定[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=435 宮内踊]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 == その他 == * [[2021年]]1月15日から22日にかけて、神社の拝殿や回廊の柱などに何者かが線状の傷をつけていたことが発覚。同年2月に[[松山城 (伊予国)|松山城]]や[[高知城]]に傷をつけていた容疑者が[[文化財保護法]]違反で逮捕され、吉備津神社でも同様の犯行を行っていたとして再逮捕されている{{Cite web|和書|date=2021-02-13 |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210213122041/https://www.jiji.com/jc/article?k=2021021300375&g=soc |title=吉備津神社に傷付けた疑い　47歳男を再逮捕―岡山県警 |publisher=時事通信|accessdate=2021-02-13}}。 == 登場作品 == * 『[[雨月物語]]』 - 墳丘長120mの[[前方後円墳]]。宮内庁により「大吉備津彦命墓」として治定されている。 ** 吉備考古館 * [[吉備津彦神社]] - 備前国一宮。 * 伝賀陽氏館跡 - 吉備津神社神官を務めた[[賀陽氏]]の館跡とされる。岡山県の指定史跡[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=325 伝賀陽氏館跡]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 * [[明菴栄西|栄西]]上人生誕地の碑 * [[造山古墳]] - （わちがい もん）]] [[File:吉備の中山 (吉備津神社から).JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|[[神体山]]とする吉備の中山}}{{small|右端は参道の松並木。}}]] [[File:Kibitsu Jinja -02.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|入り口の[[注連縄]]}}]] '''吉備津神社'''（きびつじんじゃ）は、[[岡山県]][[岡山市]][[北区 (岡山市)|北区]][[吉備津]]にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]（[[名神大社]]）、[[備中国]][[一宮]]。[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[官幣中社]]で、現在は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]。 「吉備津彦神社（きびつひこじんじゃ）」とも称したが、現在は「吉備津神社」が正式名である現在、備中・備後一宮は「吉備津神社」を名乗るが、備前一宮のみ「吉備津彦神社」を名乗る。。 == 概要 == 岡山市西部、[[備前国]]と[[備中国]]の境の[[吉備中山]]（標高175メートル）の北西麓に北面して鎮座する。吉備中山は古来[[神体山]]とされ、北東麓には備前国一宮・[[吉備津彦神社]]が鎮座する。当社と吉備津彦神社とも、主祭神に、当地を治めたとされる[[吉備津彦命|大吉備津彦命]]を祀り、命の一族を配祀する。 本来は[[吉備国]]の総鎮守であったが、吉備国の三国への分割により備中国の一宮とされ、分霊が備前国・[[備後国]]の一宮（備前：[[吉備津彦神社]]、備後：[[吉備津神社 (福山市)|吉備津神社]]）となったとされる。この事から備中の吉備津神社は「吉備総鎮守」「三備一宮」を名乗る{{Cite book |和書 |title=まいられぇ岡山 2016年版|publisher=[[山陽新聞社]] |year=2016 |page=54}}なお備前の吉備津彦神社側では、分霊による創建の伝承はない。。 [[足利義満]]造営とされる本殿は全国唯一の[[比翼入母屋造]]（吉備津造）で、拝殿とともに[[国宝]]に指定。また社殿3棟が国の[[重要文化財]]に指定されている。釜の鳴る音で吉凶を占う[[鳴釜神事]]でも有名である。 当地出身の政治家[[犬養毅]]は、犬養家遠祖の犬飼健命が大吉備津彦命の随神であるとして、吉備津神社を崇敬したという{{Cite web|和書|url=https://okayama-kanko.net/sightseeing/_cms/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/85ba4c00217acc9f333e2c3496cdce52.pdf|title=吉備路周遊マップ|publisher=公益社団法人おかやま観光コンベンション協会|date=|accessdate=2025-01-13|page=9-10}}。神池の畔に犬養毅の銅像が建てられ、吉備津神社の社号標も同人の揮毫によるものである。 [[ウメ]]、[[ツバキ]]、[[サクラ]]、[[ボタン (植物)|ボタン]]、[[ツツジ]]、[[サツキ]]、[[ハナショウブ]]、[[アジサイ]]など花の名所でもある。また[[イチョウ]]の[[紅葉]]の名所としても知られる。 == 祭神 == 祭神は次の9柱。 ; 主祭神 :* [[吉備津彦命|大吉備津彦命]]（おおきびつひこのみこと） :*: 第7代[[孝霊天皇]]の第三皇子で、元の名を「彦五十狭芹彦命（ひこいせさりひこのみこと、五十狭芹彦命）」。[[崇神天皇]]10年、[[四道将軍]]の1人として山陽道に派遣され、弟の若日子建吉備津彦命と吉備を平定した。その子孫が吉備の[[国造]]となり、古代豪族の[[吉備氏|吉備臣]]になったとされる。 ; 相殿神 :* 百田弓矢比売命（ももたゆみやひめのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の后。 :* [[御友別命]]（みともわけのみことのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の子孫。 :* 仲彦命（なかつひこのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の子孫。 :* [[千千速比売命|千々速比売命]]（ちちはやひめのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の姉。 :* [[倭迹迹日百襲姫命]]（やまとととひももそひめのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の姉。 :* 日子刺肩別命（ひこさすかたわけのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の兄。 :* [[倭迹迹稚屋姫命|倭迹迹日稚屋媛命]]（やまとととひわかやひめのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の妹。 :* [[彦狭島命|彦寤間命]]（ひこさめまのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の弟。 :* [[稚武彦命|若日子建吉備津日子命]]（わかひこたけきびつひこのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の弟。 古くは「吉備津五所大明神」として、正宮と他の4社の5社で1つの神社を成した（他4社の祭神は後述の「[[吉備津神社#摂末社|摂末社]]」項参照）。

{{clear}} == 歴史 == === 創建 === 社伝によれば、祭神の大吉備津彦命は吉備中山の麓の茅葺宮に住み、281歳で亡くなって山頂に葬られたという。吉備津神社の創建については、[[仁徳天皇]]が大吉備津彦命の功績を称えて創建したとの説がある一方、社伝では5代目の子孫の加夜臣奈留美命が茅葺宮に社殿を造営し、命を祀ったのが始まりであるとする。 === 概史 === [[朝廷 (日本)|朝廷]]からの篤い崇敬を受け、国史では[[承和 (日本)|承和]]14年（[[847年]]）に従四位下の[[神階]]を受けた記載が最初で、翌年には従四位上に進んだ。[[仁寿]]2年（[[852年]]）には神階が[[品位 (位階)|品位]]（ほんい）に変わって四品（しほん）が授けられ、[[10世紀]]には一品（いっぽん）まで昇叙された。 [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）成立の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]では[[備中国]][[賀夜郡]]に「吉備津彦神社 名神大」と記載され、[[名神大社]]に列している[[皇學館大学]]出版部『式内社調査報告 第二十二巻 山陽道』。。 中世には武家の崇敬を受け、たびたび社殿の修復や社領の寄進があった。[[江戸]]中期には[[三重塔]]を破却し神仏分離を行った。 [[明治維新]]後、[[明治]]4年（[[1871年]]）に[[近代社格制度]]において[[国幣中社]]に列し、公称を現在の「吉備津神社」に定めた。[[大正]]3年（[[1914年]]）には[[官幣中社]]に昇格した。 === 神階 === * 六国史時代における神階奉叙の記録 ** [[承和 (日本)|承和]]14年（[[847年]]）10月22日、無位から従四位下 （『[[続日本後紀]]』） - 表記は「吉備津彦命神」。 ** [[嘉祥]]元年（[[848年]]）2月21日、従四位上 （『続日本後紀』） - 表記は「吉備津彦命神」。 ** [[仁寿]]2年（[[852年]]）2月20日、四品、官社に列す （『[[日本文徳天皇実録]]』） - 表記は「吉備津彦命神」。 ** 仁寿2年（852年）8月27日時点、四品 （『日本文徳天皇実録』） - 表記は「吉備津彦命神」。 ** [[天安 (日本)|天安]]元年（[[857年]]）6月3日、四品から三品 （『日本文徳天皇実録』） - 表記は「吉備津彦命神」。 ** [[天安 (日本)|天安]]3年（[[859年]]）1月27日、三品から二品 （『[[日本三代実録]]』） - 表記は「吉備都彦命」。 * 六国史以後 ** [[天慶]]3年（[[940年]]）、一品 == 境内 == === 本殿および拝殿 === [[File:Kibitsu Jinja -01.jpg|thumb|400px|right|{{center|本殿と拝殿（国宝）}}]] 現存する本殿・拝殿は、[[室町時代]]の[[明徳]]元年（[[1390年]]）、[[後光厳天皇]]の命を受けた[[室町幕府]]3代将軍の[[足利義満]]が造営を開始し、[[応永]]32年（1425年）に遷座した[http://www.kibitujinja.com/about/honden.html 神社公式サイト]、[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=4 「おかやまの文化財」]（岡山県サイト）、[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/195650 文化遺産オンライン]などは本殿建立年代を応永32年（1425年）としている。『週刊朝日百科 日本の国宝』29号（朝日新聞社、1997）は、本殿は応永12年（1405年）に完成し、応永32年に屋根の仮葺きを檜皮葺きに改めて正式に遷宮したとする。。比翼入母屋造の本殿の手前に切妻造、平入りの拝殿が接続する。比翼入母屋造とは、[[入母屋造]]の屋根を前後に2つ並べた屋根形式で、「吉備津造」ともいう。 本殿の大きさは、[[出雲大社]]本殿、[[八坂神社]]本殿に匹敵するもので、随所に仏教建築の影響がみられる。地面より一段高く、漆喰塗の土壇（亀腹）の上に建ち、平面は桁行正面五間、背面七間、梁間八間で、屋根は[[檜皮葺]]とする。内部は中央に閉鎖的な内々陣とその手前の内陣があり、その周囲を一段低い中陣とし、中陣の手前はさらに一段低い朱の壇（あけのだん）とし、これらの周囲にさらに低い外陣が一周する。このように、外側から内側へ向けて徐々に床高を高くする特異な構造である。壁面上半には神社には珍しい連子窓をめぐらす。挿肘木、皿斗、虹梁の形状など、神社本殿に[[大仏様]]（だいぶつよう）を応用した唯一の例とされる。 拝殿は本殿と同時に造営され、桁行（側面）三間、梁間（正面）一間妻入りで、正面は切妻造、背面は本殿に接続。正面と側面には裳階（もこし）を設ける。屋根は本殿と同じく檜皮葺だが、裳階は本瓦葺きとする。これら本殿・拝殿は、合わせて1棟として[[国宝]]に指定されている『週刊朝日百科 日本の国宝』29号、朝日新聞社、1997、pp.'''2''' - 281 - '''2''' - 283。 === その他の社殿 === * 御釜殿 *: [[江戸時代]]、[[慶長]]11年（[[1606年]]）の鉱山師・安原知種による再建。単層入母屋造の平入で、本瓦葺。南北に伸びた長方形で、北二間に釜を置く。金曜日を除く毎日、特殊神事の「[[鳴釜神事]]」が行われる。国の重要文化財に指定されている。 * 回廊 *: [[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]、[[天正]]年間（[[1573年]] - [[1591年]]）の造営とされる。総延長398メートル。岡山県指定文化財に指定されている。 * 北随神門 *: 室町時代、[[天文 (元号)|天文]]11年（[[1542年]]）の再建。単層[[入母屋造]]檜皮葺。神社正面からの参道途中に建てられている。国の重要文化財に指定されている。 * 南随神門 *: [[南北朝時代 (日本)|南北朝時代]]、[[延文]]2年（[[1357年]]）の再建。吉備津神社では最古。単層入母屋造本瓦葺。本宮社への回廊途中に建てられている。国の重要文化財に指定されている。 File:吉備津神社 御釜殿.JPG|御釜殿（国の重要文化財） File:Kibitsu Jinja Corridor 03.JPG|回廊 File:吉備津神社 北随神門.JPG|北随神門（国の重要文化財） File:Kibitujinja5024.JPG|参道と二の鳥居 File:吉備津神社 一の鳥居.JPG|一の鳥居 == 摂末社 == [[File:本宮社 (吉備津神社境内社).JPG|right|thumb|200px|{{center|本宮社}}]] 古くは5つの社殿と72の末社があったとされる。5つの社殿（本社正宮・本宮社・新宮社・内宮社・岩山宮）を「吉備津五所大明神」と総称した『岡山県の地名』吉備津彦神社項。。現在、新宮社と内宮社は本宮社に合祀されている。 * 本宮社 - 五所大明神の1社。祭神：[[孝霊天皇]]（第7代。大吉備津彦命の父）。 ** 新宮社 - 五所大明神の1社。祭神：吉備武彦命（若日子建吉備津日子命の子）。本宮社に合祀。明治末までは南方の東山に鎮座。 ** 内宮社 - 五所大明神の1社。祭神：百田弓矢比売命（大吉備津彦命の妃）。本宮社に合祀。元は吉備の中山の南部山上に鎮座。 * 三社宮 - 次の3社を総称。 ** 春日宮 ** 大神宮 ** 八幡宮 * 岩山宮 - 五所大明神の1社。祭神：建日方別命（吉備国の地主神）。 * 滝祭神社 * えびす社 * 祖霊社 * 一童社 * 宇賀神社 - 神池の島に鎮座。 File:三社宮 (吉備津神社境内社).JPG|三社宮（左から春日宮、大神宮、八幡宮） File:Kibitujinja5113.JPG|岩山宮 File:Kibitsu Jinja 12.JPG|えびす社 File:Kibitujinja5117.JPG|祖霊社 File:Kibitujinja5174.JPG|一童社 File:宇賀神社 (吉備津神社境内社).JPG|宇賀神社 == 主な祭事 == {{hidden begin |title = 年間祭事一覧 |border = #aaa solid 1px |titlestyle = text-align: center; background:lightgrey; }} * 毎月 ** 月旦祭 （1日） ** 月次祭 （13日） * 1月 ** 歳旦祭 （[[1月1日]]） * 2月 ** 節分の日祭 （[[2月3日]]） ** 建国記念の日の祭 （[[2月11日]]） * 5月 ** 春季大祭 （5月第2日曜） ** 木堂祭 （[[5月15日]]） * 6月 ** 大祓式 （[[6月30日]]） * 7月 ** 夏祭り （[[7月31日]]） * 10月 ** 秋季大祭 （10月第2日曜） * 12月 ** 大祓式・除夜祭 （[[12月31日]]） {{hidden end}} == 文化財 == === 国宝 === * 本殿及び拝殿（附 棟札［明和6年］、棟札［弘化2年］）（建造物） *: 室町時代中期、応永32年（1425年）の造営。本殿・拝殿合わせて1棟として指定。明治35年4月17日に当時の[[古社寺保存法]]に基づき特別保護建造物に指定、昭和27年3月29日に[[文化財保護法]]に基づき国宝に指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|102|2993|吉備津神社本殿及び拝殿}}
[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=4 吉備津神社本殿及び拝殿]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 === 重要文化財（国指定） === * 南随神門（建造物） *: 室町時代前期、延文2年（1357年）の造営。明治44年4月17日指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|102|2994|吉備津神社南随神門}}
[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=5 吉備津神社南随身門]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 * 北随神門（建造物） *: 室町時代後期、天文12年（1543年）の造営。大正2年4月14日指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|102|2995|吉備津神社北随神門}}
[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=6 吉備津神社北随身門]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 * 御釜殿（建造物） *: 江戸時代、慶長17年（1612年）の造営。昭和55年1月26日指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|102|2996|吉備津神社御釜殿}}
[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=7 吉備津神社御釜殿]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 * 木造獅子狛犬 1対（彫刻） *: 鎌倉時代後期から南北朝にかけての作。本殿内々陣の東西に安置される。平成14年6月26日指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|10545|木造獅子狛犬}}
[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=518 木造獅子狛犬]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 === 重要無形民俗文化財（国指定） === * [[備中神楽]] *: 備中地方各地で奉納される神楽で、吉備津神社では毎月10日の[[えびす祭]]で演じられる。保護団体は備中神楽保存会。昭和54年2月3日指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|302|120|備中神楽}}
[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=319 備中神楽]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 === 岡山県指定文化財 === * 重要文化財（有形文化財） ** 回廊（建造物） - 戦国時代、天正年間（1573-1591年）の造営。昭和51年3月27日指定[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=169 吉備津神社回廊]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 ** 大太刀 銘 備州長船秀幸（工芸品） - 室町時代、長禄3年（1459年）の作。岡山県立博物館に寄託。昭和57年4月9日指定[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=700 大太刀　銘備州長船秀幸]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。刃長127.2cm、反り3.9cm。鎬造り、庵棟。秀幸は、小反り派と呼ばれる[[長船派]]傍流の刀工の中でも代表的な人物。 ** 大太刀 法光（工芸品） - 室町時代、文安3年（1446年）の作。[[岡山県立博物館]]に寄託。平成6年4月5日指定[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=701 大太刀　法光]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。全長377.3cm、刃長226.7cm、反り5cm、重量13㎏。鎬造り、丸棟。古刀期では国内最大の日本刀。奉納刀で使用した形跡は無いが、刃全体に焼入れを施し、[[茎 (刀)|茎]]が長く、3つの目釘孔が均等に空いており、実戦を意識して制作されたことがわかる。 ** 行道面（工芸品） - 岡山県立博物館に寄託。昭和34年3月27日指定[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=699 行道面]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 ** 高麗版一切経（書跡・典籍） - 朝鮮の高麗時代の経典。昭和34年3月27日指定[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=594 高麗版一切経]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 ** 紙本墨書連歌（書跡・典籍） - 応永8年（1401年）に吉備津神社で行われた法楽連歌の発句を集めたもの。昭和34年3月27日指定[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=764 本墨書連歌]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 * 無形民俗文化財 ** 宮内踊 - 門前町の宮内地区で[[7月31日]]に行われる。昭和34年3月27日指定[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=435 宮内踊]（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 == 備考 == * [[2021年]]1月15日から22日にかけて、神社の拝殿や回廊の柱などに何者かが線状の傷をつけていたことが発覚。同年2月に[[松山城 (伊予国)|松山城]]や[[高知城]]に傷をつけていた容疑者が[[文化財保護法]]違反で逮捕され、吉備津神社でも同様の犯行を行っていたとして再逮捕されている{{Cite web|和書|date=2021-02-13 |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210213122041/https://www.jiji.com/jc/article?k=2021021300375&g=soc |title=吉備津神社に傷付けた疑い　47歳男を再逮捕―岡山県警 |publisher=時事通信|accessdate=2021-02-13}}。 == 登場作品 == * 『[[雨月物語]]』 - （わちがい もん）]] [[File:吉備の中山 (吉備津神社から).JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|[[神体山]]とする吉備の中山}}{{small|右端は参道の松並木。}}]] [[File:Kibitsu Jinja -02.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|入り口の[[注連縄]]}}]] '''吉備津神社'''（きびつじんじゃ）は、[[岡山県]][[岡山市]][[北区 (岡山市)|北区]][[吉備津]]にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]（[[名神大社]]）、[[備中国]][[一宮]]。[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[官幣中社]]で、現在は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]。 「吉備津彦神社（きびつひこじんじゃ）」とも称したが、現在は「吉備津神社」が正式名である現在、備中・備後一宮は「吉備津神社」を名乗るが、備前一宮のみ「吉備津彦神社」を名乗る。。 == 概要 == 岡山市西部、[[備前国]]と[[備中国]]の境の[[吉備中山]]（標高175メートル）の北西麓に北面して鎮座する。吉備中山は古来[[神体山]]とされ、北東麓には備前国一宮・[[吉備津彦神社]]が鎮座する。当社と吉備津彦神社とも、主祭神に、当地を治めたとされる[[吉備津彦命|大吉備津彦命]]を祀り、命の一族を配祀する。 本来は[[吉備国]]の総鎮守であったが、吉備国の三国への分割により備中国の一宮とされ、分霊が備前国・[[備後国]]の一宮（備前：[[吉備津彦神社]]、備後：[[吉備津神社 (福山市)|吉備津神社]]）となったとされる。この事から備中の吉備津神社は「吉備総鎮守」「三備一宮」を名乗る{{Cite book |和書 |title=まいられぇ岡山 2016年版|publisher=[[山陽新聞社]] |year=2016 |page=54}}なお備前の吉備津彦神社側では、分霊による創建の伝承はない。。 [[足利義満]]造営とされる本殿は全国唯一の[[比翼入母屋造]]（吉備津造）で、拝殿とともに[[国宝]]に指定。また社殿3棟が国の[[重要文化財]]に指定されている。釜の鳴る音で吉凶を占う[[鳴釜神事]]でも有名である。 当地出身の政治家[[犬養毅]]は、犬養家遠祖の犬飼健命が大吉備津彦命の随神であるとして、吉備津神社を崇敬したという{{Cite web|和書|url=https://okayama-kanko.net/sightseeing/_cms/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/85ba4c00217acc9f333e2c3496cdce52.pdf|title=吉備路周遊マップ|publisher=公益社団法人おかやま観光コンベンション協会|date=|accessdate=2025-01-13|page=9-10}}。神池の畔に犬養毅の銅像が建てられ、吉備津神社の社号標も同人の揮毫によるものである。 [[ウメ]]、[[ツバキ]]、[[サクラ]]、[[ボタン (植物)|ボタン]]、[[ツツジ]]、[[サツキ]]、[[ハナショウブ]]、[[アジサイ]]など花の名所でもある。また[[イチョウ]]の[[紅葉]]の名所としても知られる。 == 祭神 == 祭神は次の9柱。 ; 主祭神 :* [[吉備津彦命|大吉備津彦命]]（おおきびつひこのみこと） :*: 第7代[[孝霊天皇]]の第三皇子で、元の名を「彦五十狭芹彦命（ひこいせさりひこのみこと、五十狭芹彦命）」。[[崇神天皇]]10年、[[四道将軍]]の1人として山陽道に派遣され、弟の若日子建吉備津彦命と吉備を平定した。その子孫が吉備の[[国造]]となり、古代豪族の[[吉備氏|吉備臣]]になったとされる。 ; 相殿神 :* 百田弓矢比売命（ももたゆみやひめのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の后。 :* [[御友別命]]（みともわけのみことのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の子孫。 :* 仲彦命（なかつひこのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の子孫。 :* [[千千速比売命|千々速比売命]]（ちちはやひめのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の姉。 :* [[倭迹迹日百襲姫命]]（やまとととひももそひめのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の姉。 :* 日子刺肩別命（ひこさすかたわけのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の兄。 :* [[倭迹迹稚屋姫命|倭迹迹日稚屋媛命]]（やまとととひわかやひめのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の妹。 :* [[彦狭島命|彦寤間命]]（ひこさめまのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の弟。 :* [[稚武彦命|若日子建吉備津日子命]]（わかひこたけきびつひこのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の弟。 古くは「吉備津五所大明神」として、正宮と他の4社の5社で1つの神社を成した（他4社の祭神は後述の「[[吉備津神社#摂末社|摂末社]]」項参照）。
