[[commons:Category:Kibitsu Jinja]][[de:Kibitsu-Schrein]][[en:Kibitsu Shrine (Bitchū)]][[eu:Kibitsu santutegia]][[fr:Kibitsu-jinja]][[ja:吉備津神社]][[ko:기비쓰 신사]][[ru:Кибицу-дзиндзя]][[vi:Điện thờ Kibitsu]][[zh:吉備津神社]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q712824]] Wikidata name: Kibitsu Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:30, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q712824]] Wikidata name: Kibitsu Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 04:10, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Okayama Prefecture, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=November 2019}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Kibitsu Jinja
吉備津神社 | image = File:Kibitsu Jinja 10.JPG | caption = [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]] (1425), a [[:en:National Treasure (Japan)|National Treasure]] {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{Coord|34.67083333|N|133.85083333|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = Kibitsu Jinja | religious_affiliation = {{ill|Shinto|qid=Q812767}} | type = | deity = {{ill|Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto|qid=Q65318}} | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 931 Kibitsu, Kita-ku, Okayama-shi, Okayama-ken 701-1341 | website = {{official|1=https://kibitujinja.com}} | architecture_style = | festivals = Second Sunday in May and October 15th each year | leadership = | footnotes = | location = {{ill|Kibitsu|qid=Q11412649}} }} {{nihongo|'''Kibitsu Jinja'''|吉備津神社}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] in the Kibitsu neighborhood of [[:en:Kita-ku, Okayama|Kita-ku, Okayama]] in [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' (first shrine) of former [[:en:Bitchū Province|Bitchū Province]]. The shrine’s main festivals are held on the second Sunday in May and October 15th each year.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} ==Overview== The Kibitsu Jinja is located in the western part of Okayama city, facing north at the northwestern foot of Mount Kibi-Nakayama (elevation 175 meters) on the border between former [[:en:Bizen Province|Bizen Province]] and Bitchū Province. The mountain has been worshipped as a [[:en:Sacred mountains|Sacred mountains]] from ancient times, and both the Kibitsu Jinja and [[Kibitsuhiko Shrine|Kibitsuhiko Jinja]] are located at its northeastern foot. Kibitsu Jinja was originally the general guardian of [[:en:Kibi Province|Kibi Province]], but due to the division of Kibi Province into three provinces, it became the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of Bitchū, and ''[[bunrei]]'' from this shrine created the ''ichinomiya'' of Bizen Province (Kibitsuhiko Jinja) and [[:en:Bingo Province|Bingo Province]] (Kibitsu Shrine). The [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]], which was re-built by [[:en:Ashikaga Yoshimitsu|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]], is a [[:en:National Treasure (Japan)|National Treasure]] and the sole exemplar of the ''[[kibitsu-zukuri]]'' style of [[:en:Japanese architecture|architecture]], although the [[Dō (architecture)|Soshidō]] of [[:en:Hokekyō-ji (Ichikawa)|Hokekyō-ji]] is now believed to have been modeled thereon.{{cite web |url=http://www.aisf.or.jp/~jaanus/deta/k/kibitsuzukuri.htm |title=Kibitsu-zukuri |publisher=[[Japanese Architecture and Art Net Users System]] |access-date=4 May 2011}}{{cite book |title=Architectural Preservation in Japan |author=Larsen, Knut Einar |publisher=[[ICOMOS]] International Wood Committee |year=1994 |pages=121–5 |isbn=82-519-1432-9}} In addition, the three shrine buildings are designated as National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]], and a special Shinto ritual "Narukama Shinto" is famous. === Mizuko and Sorei syncretism === The Shrine has a unique dual worship of [[Sorei]] or ancestral spirits alongside [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko kuyō]]{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=239}} or cults of miscarried babies. The shrine started as a place for the Kibi clan. It has the clan's ancestors as gods. This gives the shrine a pure and protective feel. The ancestors are seen as good and helpful spirits. This is how the shrine connects with [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] means the souls of babies who died early or were not born.{{Rp|page=239}} The shrine places the [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] shrine next to the ancestor shrine. It also uses running water. This setup has several meanings:{{Rp|page=239}} # The water purifies the souls of [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] is linked to water.{{Rp|page=239}} # Being near the ancestor shrine suggests these souls become kind and protective spirits.{{Rp|page=239}} # As protective spirits, the [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] guard those who remember them.{{Rp|page=239}} This way, the Kibitsu Shrine uses its ties to the Kibi clan. It creates a respectful place for [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. It links them to the shrine's ancestral and protective gods.{{Rp|page=239}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Kibitsu Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]]'''|吉備津彦命|}}, the son of [[:en:Emperor Kōrei|Emperor Kōrei]] and conqueror of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]] and founder of the [[Kibi clan]] * {{nihongo|'''Mitomowake-no-mikoto'''| 御友別命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Nakatsuhiko-no-mikoto| 仲彦命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Chichihaya-hime-no-mikoto'''|千々速比売命|}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Yamato-totohimomoso-hime-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日百襲姫命 |}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosasukatawake-no-mikoto'''| 日子刺肩別命|}}, elder brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosashikatawake-no-mikoto'''| 彦刺肩別命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hiko same ma no mikoto'''|彦寤間命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Wakahiko Takekibitsu Hikono-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日稚屋媛命|}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko ==History== The origins of Kibitsu Jinja are uncertain. According to the shrine's legend, it is located at the site of Kibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto's residence, where he died at the age of 281, and was buried on the summit of the mountain. Afterwards, the residence was turned into a shrine, possibly by his fifth generation descendent Narumi Kaya, or by [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]], who visited [[:en:Kibi Province|Kibi Province]] where he built several shrines to commemorate Kibitsuhiko. However, the shrine does not appear in any historical documentation until the late [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], until entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'' dated 847 and the ''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' dated 852. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'' it was given the Rank of {{nihongo|''Myōjin Taisha''|名神大社||}} and the Rank of ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of the province. From the [[:en:Kamakura Period|Kamakura]] through the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], was revered by the samurai, and there were frequent restorations of the shrine and donations of territory. {{Citation needed|date=November 2023}} During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the shrine's land became smaller. However, it still got a special land grant from the shogunate. This grant was for 160 koku of rice every year. There was a busy market near the shrine. People also visited teahouses and inns there. Inside the shrine area, there was a theater and a brothel. The shrine was a busy place along the [[:en:San'yōdō|San’yodō]] for travellers. This continued until the [[Meiji Restoration]]..{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=282}} After the [[Meiji Restoration]] in 1871, it was listed as a {{nihongo|National Shrine, 2nd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Chusha}}, and is 1914 was promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial Shrine, 2nd Rank|官幣中社|Kampei Chusha}}.{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese}}{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} The shrine is a ten-minute walk from [[:en:Kibitsu Station|Kibitsu Station]] on the [[:en:West Japan Railway Company|West Japan Railway Company]] [[:en:Kibi Line|Kibi Line]]. ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *''[[Honden]]'' and ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]]'', [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], built in 1390 and relocated their present locations in 1425.The main shrine has a ''Kibitsu-zukuri'' style roof, which consists of two [[:en:East Asian hip-and-gable roof|''Irimoya-zukuri'']] roof are lined up in front and behind. The influence of Buddhist architecture can be seen in many details of the structure.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2993 |title= 吉備津神社本殿及び拝殿|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine main hall and worship hall|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} ===Important Cultural Properties=== *{{nihongo|'''South Zuishinmon'''|南随神門||}}, [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], built in 1357.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2994 |title=吉備津神社南随神門|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine The [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]], which was re-built by [[:en:Ashikaga Yoshimitsu|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]], is a [[:en:National Treasure (Japan)|National Treasure]] and the sole exemplar of the ''[[kibitsu-zukuri]]'' style of [[:en:Japanese architecture|architecture]], although the [[Dō (architecture)|Soshidō]] of [[:en:Hokekyō-ji (Ichikawa)|Hokekyō-ji]] is now believed to have been modeled thereon.{{cite web |url=http://www.aisf.or.jp/~jaanus/deta/k/kibitsuzukuri.htm |title=Kibitsu-zukuri |publisher=[[Japanese Architecture and Art Net Users System]] |access-date=4 May 2011}}{{cite book |title=Architectural Preservation in Japan |author=Larsen, Knut Einar |publisher=[[ICOMOS]] International Wood Committee |year=1994 |pages=121–5 |isbn=82-519-1432-9}} In addition, the three shrine buildings are designated as National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]], and a special Shinto ritual "Narukama Shinto" is famous. === Mizuko and Sorei syncretism === The Shrine has a unique dual worship of [[Sorei]] or ancestral spirits alongside [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko kuyō]]{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=239}} or cults of miscarried babies. The shrine started as a place for the Kibi clan. It has the clan's ancestors as gods. This gives the shrine a pure and protective feel. The ancestors are seen as good and helpful spirits. This is how the shrine connects with [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] means the souls of babies who died early or were not born.{{Rp|page=239}} The shrine places the [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] shrine next to the ancestor shrine. It also uses running water. This setup has several meanings:{{Rp|page=239}} # The water purifies the souls of [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] is linked to water.{{Rp|page=239}} # Being near the ancestor shrine suggests these souls become kind and protective spirits.{{Rp|page=239}} # As protective spirits, the [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] guard those who remember them.{{Rp|page=239}} This way, the Kibitsu Shrine uses its ties to the Kibi clan. It creates a respectful place for [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. It links them to the shrine's ancestral and protective gods.{{Rp|page=239}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Kibitsu Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]]'''|吉備津彦命|}}, the son of [[:en:Emperor Kōrei|Emperor Kōrei]] and conqueror of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]] and founder of the [[Kibi clan]] * {{nihongo|'''Mitomowake-no-mikoto'''| 御友別命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Nakatsuhiko-no-mikoto| 仲彦命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Chichihaya-hime-no-mikoto'''|千々速比売命|}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Yamato-totohimomoso-hime-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日百襲姫命 |}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosasukatawake-no-mikoto'''| 日子刺肩別命|}}, elder brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosashikatawake-no-mikoto'''| 彦刺肩別命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hiko same ma no mikoto'''|彦寤間命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Wakahiko Takekibitsu Hikono-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日稚屋媛命|}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko ==History== The origins of Kibitsu Jinja are uncertain. According to the shrine's legend, it is located at the site of Kibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto's residence, where he died at the age of 281, and was buried on the summit of the mountain. Afterwards, the residence was turned into a shrine, possibly by his fifth generation descendent Narumi Kaya, or by [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]], who visited [[:en:Kibi Province|Kibi Province]] where he built several shrines to commemorate Kibitsuhiko. However, the shrine does not appear in any historical documentation until the late [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], until entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'' dated 847 and the ''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' dated 852. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'' it was given the Rank of {{nihongo|''Myōjin Taisha''|名神大社||}} and the Rank of ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of the province. From the [[:en:Kamakura Period|Kamakura]] through the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], was revered by the samurai, and there were frequent restorations of the shrine and donations of territory. {{Citation needed|date=November 2023}} During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the shrine's land became smaller. However, it still got a special land grant from the shogunate. This grant was for 160 koku of rice every year. There was a busy market near the shrine. People also visited teahouses and inns there. Inside the shrine area, there was a theater and a brothel. The shrine was a busy place along the [[:en:San'yōdō|San’yodō]] for travellers. This continued until the [[Meiji Restoration]]..{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=282}} After the [[Meiji Restoration]] in 1871, it was listed as a {{nihongo|National Shrine, 2nd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Chusha}}, and is 1914 was promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial Shrine, 2nd Rank|官幣中社|Kampei Chusha}}.{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese}}{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} The shrine is a ten-minute walk from [[:en:Kibitsu Station|Kibitsu Station]] on the [[:en:West Japan Railway Company|West Japan Railway Company]] [[:en:Kibi Line|Kibi Line]]. ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *''[[Honden]]'' and ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]]'', [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], built in 1390 and relocated their present locations in 1425.The main shrine has a ''Kibitsu-zukuri'' style roof, which consists of two [[:en:East Asian hip-and-gable roof|''Irimoya-zukuri'']] roof are lined up in front and behind. The influence of Buddhist architecture can be seen in many details of the structure.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2993 |title= 吉備津神社本殿及び拝殿|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine main hall and worship hall|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} ===Important Cultural Properties=== *{{nihongo|'''South Zuishinmon'''|南随神門||}}, [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], built in 1357.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2994 |title=吉備津神社南随神門|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine South Zuijinmon|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} *{{nihongo|'''North Zuishinmon'''|北随神門||}}, [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], built in [[:en:Kamakura Period|Kamakura]] to [[:en:Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-chō period]], Located to the east and west of the Honden.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/10545 [[sn:commons:Category:Kibitsu Jinja]][[de:Kibitsu-Schrein]][[en:Kibitsu Shrine (Bitchū)]][[eu:Kibitsu santutegia]][[fr:Kibitsu-jinja]][[ja:吉備津神社]][[ko:기비쓰 신사]][[ru:Кибицу-дзиндзя]][[vi:Điện thờ Kibitsu]][[zh:吉備津神社]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q712824]] Wikidata name: Kibitsu Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:30, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q712824]] Wikidata name: Kibitsu Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 04:10, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Okayama Prefecture, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=November 2019}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Kibitsu Jinja
吉備津神社 | image = File:Kibitsu Jinja 10.JPG | caption = [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]] (1425), a [[:en:National Treasure (Japan)|National Treasure]] {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{Coord|34.67083333|N|133.85083333|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = Kibitsu Jinja | religious_affiliation = {{ill|Shinto|WD=Q812767}} | type = | deity = {{ill|Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto|WD=Q65318}} | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 931 Kibitsu, Kita-ku, Okayama-shi, Okayama-ken 701-1341 | website = {{official|1=https://kibitujinja.com}} | architecture_style = | festivals = Second Sunday in May and October 15th each year | leadership = | footnotes = | location = {{ill|Kibitsu|WD=Q11412649}} }} {{nihongo|'''Kibitsu Jinja'''|吉備津神社}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] in the Kibitsu neighborhood of [[:en:Kita-ku, Okayama|Kita-ku, Okayama]] in [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' (first shrine) of former [[:en:Bitchū Province|Bitchū Province]]. The shrine’s main festivals are held on the second Sunday in May and October 15th each year.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} ==Overview== The Kibitsu Jinja is located in the western part of Okayama city, facing north at the northwestern foot of Mount Kibi-Nakayama (elevation 175 meters) on the border between former [[:en:Bizen Province|Bizen Province]] and Bitchū Province. The mountain has been worshipped as a [[:en:Sacred mountains|Sacred mountains]] from ancient times, and both the Kibitsu Jinja and [[Kibitsuhiko Shrine|Kibitsuhiko Jinja]] are located at its northeastern foot. Kibitsu Jinja was originally the general guardian of [[:en:Kibi Province|Kibi Province]], but due to the division of Kibi Province into three provinces, it became the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of Bitchū, and ''[[bunrei]]'' from this shrine created the ''ichinomiya'' of Bizen Province (Kibitsuhiko Jinja) and [[:en:Bingo Province|Bingo Province]] (Kibitsu Shrine). The [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]], which was re-built by [[:en:Ashikaga Yoshimitsu|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]], is a [[:en:National Treasure (Japan)|National Treasure]] and the sole exemplar of the ''[[kibitsu-zukuri]]'' style of [[:en:Japanese architecture|architecture]], although the [[Dō (architecture)|Soshidō]] of [[:en:Hokekyō-ji (Ichikawa)|Hokekyō-ji]] is now believed to have been modeled thereon.{{cite web |url=http://www.aisf.or.jp/~jaanus/deta/k/kibitsuzukuri.htm |title=Kibitsu-zukuri |publisher=[[Japanese Architecture and Art Net Users System]] |access-date=4 May 2011}}{{cite book |title=Architectural Preservation in Japan |author=Larsen, Knut Einar |publisher=[[ICOMOS]] International Wood Committee |year=1994 |pages=121–5 |isbn=82-519-1432-9}} In addition, the three shrine buildings are designated as National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]], and a special Shinto ritual "Narukama Shinto" is famous. === Mizuko and Sorei syncretism === The Shrine has a unique dual worship of [[Sorei]] or ancestral spirits alongside [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko kuyō]]{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=239}} or cults of miscarried babies. The shrine started as a place for the Kibi clan. It has the clan's ancestors as gods. This gives the shrine a pure and protective feel. The ancestors are seen as good and helpful spirits. This is how the shrine connects with [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] means the souls of babies who died early or were not born.{{Rp|page=239}} The shrine places the [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] shrine next to the ancestor shrine. It also uses running water. This setup has several meanings:{{Rp|page=239}} # The water purifies the souls of [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] is linked to water.{{Rp|page=239}} # Being near the ancestor shrine suggests these souls become kind and protective spirits.{{Rp|page=239}} # As protective spirits, the [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] guard those who remember them.{{Rp|page=239}} This way, the Kibitsu Shrine uses its ties to the Kibi clan. It creates a respectful place for [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. It links them to the shrine's ancestral and protective gods.{{Rp|page=239}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Kibitsu Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]]'''|吉備津彦命|}}, the son of [[:en:Emperor Kōrei|Emperor Kōrei]] and conqueror of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]] and founder of the [[Kibi clan]] * {{nihongo|'''Mitomowake-no-mikoto'''| 御友別命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Nakatsuhiko-no-mikoto| 仲彦命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Chichihaya-hime-no-mikoto'''|千々速比売命|}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Yamato-totohimomoso-hime-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日百襲姫命 |}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosasukatawake-no-mikoto'''| 日子刺肩別命|}}, elder brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosashikatawake-no-mikoto'''| 彦刺肩別命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hiko same ma no mikoto'''|彦寤間命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Wakahiko Takekibitsu Hikono-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日稚屋媛命|}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko ==History== The origins of Kibitsu Jinja are uncertain. According to the shrine's legend, it is located at the site of Kibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto's residence, where he died at the age of 281, and was buried on the summit of the mountain. Afterwards, the residence was turned into a shrine, possibly by his fifth generation descendent Narumi Kaya, or by [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]], who visited [[:en:Kibi Province|Kibi Province]] where he built several shrines to commemorate Kibitsuhiko. However, the shrine does not appear in any historical documentation until the late [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], until entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'' dated 847 and the ''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' dated 852. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'' it was given the Rank of {{nihongo|''Myōjin Taisha''|名神大社||}} and the Rank of ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of the province. From the [[:en:Kamakura Period|Kamakura]] through the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], was revered by the samurai, and there were frequent restorations of the shrine and donations of territory. {{Citation needed|date=November 2023}} During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the shrine's land became smaller. However, it still got a special land grant from the shogunate. This grant was for 160 koku of rice every year. There was a busy market near the shrine. People also visited teahouses and inns there. Inside the shrine area, there was a theater and a brothel. The shrine was a busy place along the [[:en:San'yōdō|San’yodō]] for travellers. This continued until the [[Meiji Restoration]]..{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=282}} After the [[Meiji Restoration]] in 1871, it was listed as a {{nihongo|National Shrine, 2nd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Chusha}}, and is 1914 was promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial Shrine, 2nd Rank|官幣中社|Kampei Chusha}}.{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese}}{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} The shrine is a ten-minute walk from [[:en:Kibitsu Station|Kibitsu Station]] on the [[:en:West Japan Railway Company|West Japan Railway Company]] [[:en:Kibi Line|Kibi Line]]. ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *''[[Honden]]'' and ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]]'', [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], built in 1390 and relocated their present locations in 1425.The main shrine has a ''Kibitsu-zukuri'' style roof, which consists of two [[:en:East Asian hip-and-gable roof|''Irimoya-zukuri'']] roof are lined up in front and behind. The influence of Buddhist architecture can be seen in many details of the structure.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2993 |title= 吉備津神社本殿及び拝殿|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine main hall and worship hall|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} ===Important Cultural Properties=== *{{nihongo|'''South Zuishinmon'''|南随神門||}}, [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], built in 1357.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2994 |title=吉備津神社南随神門|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine South Zuijinmon|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} *{{nihongo|'''North Zuishinmon'''|北随神門||}}, [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], built in 1543.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2995 |title=吉備津神社北随神門|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine North Zuijinmon|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} *{{nihongo|'''Okama-den'''|御釜殿||}}, [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], built in 1612.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2996 |title= 吉備津神社御釜殿|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine Okamaden|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} *{{nihongo|'''Komainu'''|木造獅子狛犬||}}, one pair, late [[:en:Kamakura Period|Kamakura]] to [[:en:Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-chō period]], Located to the east and west of the Honden.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/10545 |title= 木造獅子狛犬|trans-title=Mokuzō shishi komainu|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} ==Gallery== File:吉備津神社 御釜殿.JPG|Okamaden（ICP） File:Kibitsu [[sn:commons:Category:Kibitsu Jinja]][[de:Kibitsu-Schrein]][[en:Kibitsu Shrine (Bitchū)]][[eu:Kibitsu santutegia]][[fr:Kibitsu-jinja]][[ja:吉備津神社]][[ko:기비쓰 신사]][[ru:Кибицу-дзиндзя]][[vi:Điện thờ Kibitsu]][[zh:吉備津神社]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q712824]] Wikidata name: Kibitsu Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:30, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q712824]] Wikidata name: Kibitsu Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 04:10, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Okayama Prefecture, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=November 2019}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Kibitsu Jinja
吉備津神社 | image = File:Kibitsu Jinja 10.JPG | caption = [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]] (1425), a [[:en:National Treasure (Japan)|National Treasure]] {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{Coord|34.67083333|N|133.85083333|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = Kibitsu Jinja | religious_affiliation = {{ill|Shinto|WD=Q812767}} | type = | deity = {{ill|Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto|WD=Q65318}} | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 931 Kibitsu, Kita-ku, Okayama-shi, Okayama-ken 701-1341 | website = {{official|1=https://kibitujinja.com}} | architecture_style = | festivals = Second Sunday in May and October 15th each year | leadership = | footnotes = | location = {{ill|Kibitsu|WD=Q11412649}} }} {{nihongo|'''Kibitsu Jinja'''|吉備津神社}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] in the Kibitsu neighborhood of [[:en:Kita-ku, Okayama|Kita-ku, Okayama]] in [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' (first shrine) of former [[:en:Bitchū Province|Bitchū Province]]. The shrine’s main festivals are held on the second Sunday in May and October 15th each year.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} ==Overview== The Kibitsu Jinja is located in the western part of Okayama city, facing north at the northwestern foot of Mount Kibi-Nakayama (elevation 175 meters) on the border between former [[:en:Bizen Province|Bizen Province]] and Bitchū Province. The mountain has been worshipped as a [[:en:Sacred mountains|Sacred mountains]] from ancient times, and both the Kibitsu Jinja and [[Kibitsuhiko Shrine|Kibitsuhiko Jinja]] are located at its northeastern foot. Kibitsu Jinja was originally the general guardian of [[:en:Kibi Province|Kibi Province]], but due to the division of Kibi Province into three provinces, it became the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of Bitchū, and ''[[bunrei]]'' from this shrine created the ''ichinomiya'' of Bizen Province (Kibitsuhiko Jinja) and [[:en:Bingo Province|Bingo Province]] (Kibitsu Shrine). The [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]], which was re-built by [[:en:Ashikaga Yoshimitsu|Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]], is a [[:en:National Treasure (Japan)|National Treasure]] and the sole exemplar of the ''[[kibitsu-zukuri]]'' style of [[:en:Japanese architecture|architecture]], although the [[Dō (architecture)|Soshidō]] of [[:en:Hokekyō-ji (Ichikawa)|Hokekyō-ji]] is now believed to have been modeled thereon.{{cite web |url=http://www.aisf.or.jp/~jaanus/deta/k/kibitsuzukuri.htm |title=Kibitsu-zukuri |publisher=[[Japanese Architecture and Art Net Users System]] |access-date=4 May 2011}}{{cite book |title=Architectural Preservation in Japan |author=Larsen, Knut Einar |publisher=[[ICOMOS]] International Wood Committee |year=1994 |pages=121–5 |isbn=82-519-1432-9}} In addition, the three shrine buildings are designated as National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]], and a special Shinto ritual "Narukama Shinto" is famous. === Mizuko and Sorei syncretism === The Shrine has a unique dual worship of [[Sorei]] or ancestral spirits alongside [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko kuyō]]{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=239}} or cults of miscarried babies. The shrine started as a place for the Kibi clan. It has the clan's ancestors as gods. This gives the shrine a pure and protective feel. The ancestors are seen as good and helpful spirits. This is how the shrine connects with [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] means the souls of babies who died early or were not born.{{Rp|page=239}} The shrine places the [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] shrine next to the ancestor shrine. It also uses running water. This setup has several meanings:{{Rp|page=239}} # The water purifies the souls of [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] is linked to water.{{Rp|page=239}} # Being near the ancestor shrine suggests these souls become kind and protective spirits.{{Rp|page=239}} # As protective spirits, the [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] guard those who remember them.{{Rp|page=239}} This way, the Kibitsu Shrine uses its ties to the Kibi clan. It creates a respectful place for [[:en:Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. It links them to the shrine's ancestral and protective gods.{{Rp|page=239}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Kibitsu Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]]'''|吉備津彦命|}}, the son of [[:en:Emperor Kōrei|Emperor Kōrei]] and conqueror of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]] and founder of the [[Kibi clan]] * {{nihongo|'''Mitomowake-no-mikoto'''| 御友別命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Nakatsuhiko-no-mikoto| 仲彦命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Chichihaya-hime-no-mikoto'''|千々速比売命|}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Yamato-totohimomoso-hime-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日百襲姫命 |}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosasukatawake-no-mikoto'''| 日子刺肩別命|}}, elder brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosashikatawake-no-mikoto'''| 彦刺肩別命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hiko same ma no mikoto'''|彦寤間命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Wakahiko Takekibitsu Hikono-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日稚屋媛命|}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko ==History== The origins of Kibitsu Jinja are uncertain. According to the shrine's legend, it is located at the site of Kibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto's residence, where he died at the age of 281, and was buried on the summit of the mountain. Afterwards, the residence was turned into a shrine, possibly by his fifth generation descendent Narumi Kaya, or by [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]], who visited [[:en:Kibi Province|Kibi Province]] where he built several shrines to commemorate Kibitsuhiko. However, the shrine does not appear in any historical documentation until the late [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], until entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'' dated 847 and the ''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' dated 852. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'' it was given the Rank of {{nihongo|''Myōjin Taisha''|名神大社||}} and the Rank of ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of the province. From the [[:en:Kamakura Period|Kamakura]] through the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], was revered by the samurai, and there were frequent restorations of the shrine and donations of territory. {{Citation needed|date=November 2023}} During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the shrine's land became smaller. However, it still got a special land grant from the shogunate. This grant was for 160 koku of rice every year. There was a busy market near the shrine. People also visited teahouses and inns there. Inside the shrine area, there was a theater and a brothel. The shrine was a busy place along the [[:en:San'yōdō|San’yodō]] for travellers. This continued until the [[Meiji Restoration]]..{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=282}} After the [[Meiji Restoration]] in 1871, it was listed as a {{nihongo|National Shrine, 2nd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Chusha}}, and is 1914 was promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial Shrine, 2nd Rank|官幣中社|Kampei Chusha}}.{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese}}{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} The shrine is a ten-minute walk from [[:en:Kibitsu Station|Kibitsu Station]] on the [[:en:West Japan Railway Company|West Japan Railway Company]] [[:en:Kibi Line|Kibi Line]]. ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *''[[Honden]]'' and ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]]'', [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], built in 1390 and relocated their present locations in 1425.The main shrine has a ''Kibitsu-zukuri'' style roof, which consists of two [[:en:East Asian hip-and-gable roof|''Irimoya-zukuri'']] roof are lined up in front and behind. The influence of Buddhist architecture can be seen in many details of the structure.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2993 |title= 吉備津神社本殿及び拝殿|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine main hall and worship hall|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} ===Important Cultural Properties=== *{{nihongo|'''South Zuishinmon'''|南随神門||}}, [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], built in 1357.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2994 |title=吉備津神社南随神門|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine South Zuijinmon|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} *{{nihongo|'''North Zuishinmon'''|北随神門||}}, [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], built in 1543.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2995 |title=吉備津神社北随神門|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine North Zuijinmon|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} *{{nihongo|'''Okama-den'''|御釜殿||}}, [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], built in 1612.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2996 |title= 吉備津神社御釜殿|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine Okamaden|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} *{{nihongo|'''Komainu'''|木造獅子狛犬||}}, one pair, late [[:en:Kamakura Period|Kamakura]] to [[:en:Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-chō period]], Located to the east and west of the Honden.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/10545 |title= 木造獅子狛犬|trans-title=Mokuzō shishi komainu|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} ==Gallery== File:吉備津神社 御釜殿.JPG|Okamaden（ICP） File:Kibitsu Jinja Corridor 03.JPG|Cloister File:吉備津神社 北随神門.JPG|North Zuijinmon（ICP） File:Kibitujinja5024.JPG|Approach and Ni-no-Torii File:吉備津神社 一の鳥居.JPG|Ichi-no-Torii ==See also== *[[:en:List of National From the [[:en:Kamakura Period|Kamakura]] through the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], was revered by the samurai, and there were frequent restorations of the shrine and donations of territory. {{Citation needed|date=November 2023}} During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the shrine's land became smaller. However, it still got a special land grant from the shogunate. This grant was for 160 koku of rice every year. There was a busy market near the shrine. People also visited teahouses and inns there. Inside the shrine area, there was a theater and a brothel. The shrine was a busy place along the [[:en:San'yōdō|San’yodō]] for travellers. This continued until the [[Meiji Restoration]]..{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=282}} After the [[Meiji Restoration]] in 1871, it was listed as a {{nihongo|National Shrine, 2nd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Chusha}}, and is 1914 was promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial Shrine, 2nd Rank|官幣中社|Kampei Chusha}}.{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese}}{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} The shrine is a ten-minute walk from [[:en:Kibitsu Station|Kibitsu Station]] on the [[:en:West Japan Railway Company|West Japan Railway Company]] [[:en:Kibi Line|Kibi Line]]. ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *''[[Honden]]'' and ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]]'', [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], built in 1390 and relocated their present locations in 1425.The main shrine has a ''Kibitsu-zukuri'' style roof, which consists of two [[:en:East Asian hip-and-gable roof|''Irimoya-zukuri'']] roof are lined up in front and behind. The influence of Buddhist architecture can be seen in many details of the structure.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2993 |title= 吉備津神社本殿及び拝殿|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine main hall and worship hall|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} ===Important Cultural Properties=== *{{nihongo|'''South Zuishinmon'''|南随神門||}}, [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], built in 1357.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2994 |title=吉備津神社南随神門|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine South Zuijinmon|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} *{{nihongo|'''North Zuishinmon'''|北随神門||}}, [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], built in 1543.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2995 |title=吉備津神社北随神門|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine North Zuijinmon|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} *{{nihongo|'''Okama-den'''|御釜殿||}}, [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], built in 1612.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2996 |title= {{otheruses|岡山県岡山市の神社|その他|吉備津神社 (曖昧さ回避)}} {{神社 |名称 = 吉備津神社 |画像 = [[File:Kibitsu Jinja 10 cropped.jpg|270px]]
本殿（国宝） |所在地 = [[岡山県]][[岡山市]][[北区 (岡山市)|北区]][[吉備津]]931 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|40|14.4|N|133|51|2.2|E|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[吉備津彦命|大吉備津彦命]] |社格 = [[式内社]]（[[名神大社|名神大]]）
[[備中国]][[一宮]]
旧[[官幣中社]]
[[別表神社]] |創建 = 不詳（[[仁徳天皇]]代） |本殿 = 吉備津造[[檜皮葺]] |神体 = [[吉備中山]]（[[神体山]]） |別名 = |札所等 = |例祭 = 5月第2日曜・[[10月19日]] |神事 = [[鳴釜神事]]（金曜以外毎日）七十五膳据神事（春・秋） |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Okayama|label=吉備津神社|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}}}} [[ファイル:Wachigai.svg|thumb|right|220px|社家賀陽家の家紋（輪違い紋）
（わちがい もん）]] [[File:Kibitsu Jinja -02.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|入り口の[[注連縄]]}}]] '''吉備津神社'''（きびつじんじゃ）は、[[岡山県]][[岡山市]][[北区 (岡山市)|北区]][[吉備津]]にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]（[[名神大社]]）、[[備中国]][[一宮]]。[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[官幣中社]]で、現在は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]。 『[[延喜式]]』では「吉備津彦神社（きびつひこじんじゃ）」と所載されている。[[2025年]]（[[令和]]7年）[[現在]]は'''「吉備津神社」が正式名'''である現在、備中・備後一宮は「吉備津神社」を名乗るが、備前一宮のみ「吉備津彦神社」を名乗る。。 == 概要 == 岡山市西部、[[備前国]]と[[備中国]]の境の[[吉備中山]]（標高175メートル）の北西麓に北面して鎮座する。吉備中山は古来[[神体山]]とされ、北東麓には備前国一宮・[[吉備津彦神社]]が鎮座する。当社と吉備津彦神社とも、主祭神に、当地を治めたとされる[[吉備津彦命|大吉備津彦命]]を祀り、命の一族を配祀する。 本来は[[吉備国]]の総鎮守であったが、吉備国の三国への分割により備中国の一宮とされ、分霊が備前国・[[備後国]]の一宮（備前：吉備津彦神社、備後：[[吉備津神社 (福山市)|吉備津神社]]）となったとされる。このことから備中の吉備津神社は「吉備総鎮守」「三備一宮」を名乗る{{Cite book |和書 |title=まいられぇ岡山 2016年版|publisher=[[山陽新聞社]] |year=2016 |page=54}}なお備前の吉備津彦神社側では、分霊による創建の伝承はない。。 [[足利義満]]造営とされる本殿は全国唯一の[[比翼入母屋造]]（吉備津造）で、拝殿とともに[[国宝]]に指定。また社殿3棟が国の[[重要文化財]]に指定されている。釜の鳴る音で吉凶を占う[[鳴釜神事]]でも有名である。 当地出身の政治家[[犬養毅]]は、犬養家遠祖の犬飼健命が大吉備津彦命の随神であるとして、吉備津神社を崇敬したという{{Cite web|和書|url=https://okayama-kanko.net/sightseeing/_cms/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/85ba4c00217acc9f333e2c3496cdce52.pdf|title=吉備路周遊マップ|publisher=公益社団法人おかやま観光コンベンション協会|date=|accessdate=2025-01-13|pages=9-10}}。神池の畔に犬養毅の銅像が建てられ、吉備津神社の社号標も同人の揮毫によるものである。 5月第2日曜日に春季大祭が、10月第2日曜日に秋季大祭が行われる。中でも七十五膳据神事は、御供殿から回廊を通って本殿まで75の膳を運び献供するもので、岡山県下三大祭りの1つである{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.okayama-kanko.jp/event/detail_12508.html|title=吉備津神社 大祭 七十五膳据神事|publisher=岡山県観光連盟|date=|accessdate=2025-11-15|pages=}}。 「[[ウメ]]」・「[[ツバキ]]」・「[[サクラ]]」・「[[ボタン (植物)|ボタン]]」・「[[ツツジ]]」・「[[サツキ]]」・「[[ハナショウブ]]」・「[[アジサイ]]」など花の名所でもある。また[[イチョウ]]の[[紅葉]]の名所としても知られる。 == 祭神 == 祭神は次の9柱。 ; 主祭神 :* [[吉備津彦命|大吉備津彦命]]（おおきびつひこのみこと） :*: 第7代[[孝霊天皇]]の第3[[皇子]]で、元の名を「彦五十狭芹彦命（ひこいさせりひこのみこと、五十狭芹彦命）」。[[崇神天皇]]10年、[[四道将軍]]の1人として山陽道に派遣され、弟の若日子建吉備津彦命と吉備を平定した。その子孫が吉備の[[国造]]となり、[[古代]][[豪族]]の[[吉備氏|吉備臣]]になったとされる。 ; 相殿神 :* 百田弓矢比売命（ももたゆみやひめのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の后。 :* [[御友別命]]（みともわけのみことのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の[[wikt:子孫|子孫]]。 :* 仲彦命（なかつひこのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の子孫。 :* [[千千速比売命|千々速比売命]]（ちちはやひめのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の[[姉]]。 :* [[倭迹迹日百襲姫命]]（やまとととひももそひめのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の姉。 :* 日子刺肩別命（ひこさすかたわけのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の[[兄]]。 :* [[倭迹迹稚屋姫命|倭迹迹日稚屋媛命]]（やまとととひわかやひめのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の[[妹]]。 :* [[彦狭島命|彦寤間命]]（ひこさめまのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の[[弟]]。 :* [[稚武彦命|若日子建吉備津日子命]]（わかひこたけきびつひこのみこと） - 大吉備津彦命の弟。 古くは「吉備津五所大明神」として、正宮と他の4社の5社で1つの神社を成した（他4社の祭神は後述の「[[吉備津神社#摂末社|摂末社]]」項参照）。
祭神の関係略図
: 社伝に従うもので、古事記・日本書紀等の系図とは表記が若干異なる。 {{familytree/start|style=font-size:90%}} {{familytree|border=0|boxstyle=text-align:left|-|01|v|02|-| 01={{sup|7}} [[孝霊天皇]]|02={{sup|8}} [[孝元天皇]]}} {{familytree|border=0|boxstyle=text-align:left| ||||)|01| 01=[[千千速比売命|千々速比売命]]}} {{familytree|border=0|boxstyle=text-align:left| ||||)|01| 01=[[倭迹迹日百襲媛命|倭迹迹日百襲姫命]]}} {{familytree|border=0|boxstyle=text-align:left| ||||)|01| 01=日子刺肩別命}} {{familytree|border=0|boxstyle=text-align:left| ||||)|01|-|02| 01='''[[吉備津彦命|大吉備津彦命]]'''|02=　→　［[[吉備氏]]］}} {{familytree|border=0|boxstyle=text-align:left| ||||)|01| 01=[[倭迹迹稚屋姫命|倭迹迹日稚屋媛命]]}} {{familytree|border=0|boxstyle=text-align:left| ||||)|01| 01=[[彦狭島命|彦寤間命]]}} {{familytree|border=0|boxstyle=text-align:left| ||||`|01|-|02| 01=[[稚武彦命|若日子建吉備津日子命]]|02=　→　［吉備氏］}} {{familytree/end}}
{{clear}} == 歴史 == === 創建 === [[File:吉備の中山 (吉備津神社から).JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|鎮座する[[吉備の中山]]}}{{small|右端は参道の松並木。}}]] 社伝によれば、祭神の大吉備津彦命は[[吉備中山]]の麓の茅葺宮に住み、281歳で[[崩御#薨去(こうきょ)|亡くなって]]山頂に葬られたという。吉備津神社の創建については、[[仁徳天皇]]が大吉備津彦命の功績を称えて創建したとの説がある一方、社伝では5代目の子孫の加夜臣奈留美命が茅葺宮に社殿を造営し、命を祀ったのが始まりであるとする。 === 概史 === [[朝廷 (日本)|朝廷]]からの篤い崇敬を受け、国史では[[承和 (日本)|承和]]14年（[[847年]]）に従四位下の[[神階]]を受けた記載が最初で、翌年には従四位上に進んだ。[[仁寿]]2年（[[852年]]）には神階が[[品位 (位階)|品位]]（ほんい）に変わって四品（しほん）が授けられ、[[10世紀]]には一品（いっぽん）まで昇叙された。 [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）成立の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]では[[備中国]][[賀夜郡]]に「吉備津彦神社 名神大」と記載され、[[名神大社]]に列している[[皇學館大学]]出版部『式内社調査報告 第二十二巻 山陽道』。。 吉備津神社に対しては[[平安時代]]初期に朝廷から[[封戸]]が当てられ、寄進地を加えながら社地は拡大し、やがて権門に寄進されて[[荘園 (日本)|荘園]]化した{{Cite journal |和書 |author= 四宮 浩 |title=近世備中国吉備津神社における神仏分離の様相 |journal= 立正大学大学院年報|volume=39 |issue= |publisher=立正大学大学院文学研究科 |date= |pages=33-48 |url=https://rissho.repo.nii.ac.jp/records/10438}}。 [[鎌倉時代]]初期になると[[仁和寺]]に寄進されてその所領となったが、[[南北朝時代 (日本)|南北朝時代]]には争乱により仁和寺の支配も脅かされた。さらに[[応仁の乱]]以降は備中国守護の[[細川氏]]や在地勢力の松田氏らに社領が支配されることもあった。 [[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]末期には[[毛利氏]]の勢力が及んで[[清水宗治]]らが実質的に支配した。さらに[[豊臣秀吉]]による国内統一後は[[宇喜田秀家]]領となって社領の寄進を受けた。なお、仁和寺との支配関係も近世初期まで継続し、特に祭祀面で影響を受けていた。 [[江戸時代]]にはひとまず[[徳川氏]]の直轄地として備中代官[[小堀正次]]の支配下となり、その後、吉備津神社のある宮内村は[[庭瀬藩]]領となった。慶長6年（[[1601年]]）4月、[[徳川家康]]から160石が寄進され、境内敷地の除地60石を差し引くと100石で、宇喜多氏時代の石高を維持した。ところが、[[朱印状]]は単に「備中国宮内神領」となっていたため宛先をめぐって神社内の社家方と社僧方の間で相論となった。寛文3年（[[1663年]]）の[[寺社奉行]]の判決で社家方が本願を管理することを認められ、寛文5年（[[1665年]]）以降の朱印状は「吉備津大明神社領」と明記された。その後も境内には[[三重塔]]などの仏教施設は残され、僧侶による神前読経も続けられていた。 しかし、享保14年（[[1729年]]）、社家方から三重塔は経年劣化により修復困難で風雨や地震の際に危険であるとして寺社奉行に撤去願いが出され、仏教側はその差し止めを求めた。両者の相論は三重塔撤去の是非だけでなく、神社が神仏習合の宮であるか、唯一神道の社として神仏習合を廃するかの議論に発展した。寺社奉行は唯一神道か否かは直接判断しなかったが、三重塔の撤去を認め、寺院側が神社に関わることを否定して提訴の資格もないと判断した。享保期以降の境内図からは三重塔などの仏教建築物がなくなっており、この時期に神仏分離が完成したとみられている。 [[明治維新]]後、[[明治]]4年（[[1871年]]）に[[近代社格制度]]において[[国幣中社]]に列し、公称を現在の「吉備津神社」に定めた。[[1914年]]（[[大正]]3年）には[[官幣中社]]に昇格した。 === 神階 === * 六国史時代における神階奉叙の記録 ** [[承和 (日本)|承和]]14年（[[847年]]）10月22日、無位から従四位下 （『[[続日本後紀]]』） - 表記は「吉備津彦命神」。 ** [[嘉祥]]元年（[[848年]]）2月21日、従四位上 （『続日本後紀』） - 表記は「吉備津彦命神」。 ** [[仁寿]]2年（[[852年]]）2月20日、四品、官社に列す （『[[日本文徳天皇実録]]』） - 表記は「吉備津彦命神」。 ** 仁寿2年（852年）8月27日時点、四品 （『日本文徳天皇実録』） - 表記は「吉備津彦命神」。 ** [[天安 (日本)|天安]]元年（[[857年]]）6月3日、四品から三品 （『日本文徳天皇実録』） - 表記は「吉備津彦命神」。 ** 天安3年（[[859年]]）1月27日、三品から二品 （『[[日本三代実録]]』） - 表記は「吉備都彦命」。 * 六国史以後 ** [[天慶]]3年（[[940年]]）、一品 == 境内 == === 本殿および拝殿 === [[File:Kibitsu Jinja -01.jpg|thumb|400px|right|{{center|本殿と拝殿（国宝）}}]] 現存する本殿・拝殿は、[[室町時代]]の[[明徳]]元年（[[1390年]]）、[[後光厳天皇]]の命を受けた[[室町幕府]]3代将軍の[[足利義満]]が造営を開始し、[[応永]]32年（1425年）に遷座した[http://www.kibitujinja.com/about/honden.html 神社公式サイト]、[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=4 「おかやまの文化財」]（岡山県サイト）、[https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/195650 文化遺産オンライン]などは本殿建立年代を応永32年（[[1425年]]）としている。『週刊朝日百科 日本の国宝』29号（朝日新聞社、1997）は、本殿は応永12年（[[1405年]]）に完成し、応永32年に屋根の仮葺きを檜皮葺きに改めて正式に遷宮したとする。。比翼入母屋造の本殿の手前に切妻造、平入りの拝殿が接続する。比翼入母屋造とは、[[入母屋造]]の屋根を前後に2つ並べた屋根形式で、「吉備津造」ともいう。 本殿の大きさは、[[出雲大社]]本殿、[[八坂神社]]本殿に匹敵するもので、随所に仏教建築の影響がみられる。地面より一段高く、漆喰塗の土壇（亀腹）の上に建ち、平面は桁行正面五間、背面七間、梁間八間で、屋根は[[檜皮葺]]とする。内部は中央に閉鎖的な内々陣とその手前の内陣があり、その周囲を一段低い中陣とし、中陣の手前はさらに一段低い朱の壇（あけのだん）とし、これらの周囲にさらに低い外陣が一周する。このように、外側から内側へ向けて徐々に床高を高くする特異な構造である。壁面上半には神社には珍しい連子窓をめぐらす。挿肘木、皿斗、虹梁の形状など、神社本殿に[[大仏様]]（だいぶつよう）を応用した唯一の例とされる。 拝殿は本殿と同時に造営され、桁行（側面）三間、梁間（正面）一間妻入りで、正面は切妻造・背面は本殿に接続。正面と側面には裳階（もこし）を設ける。屋根は本殿と同じく檜皮葺だが、裳階は本瓦葺きとする。これら本殿・拝殿は、合わせて1棟として[[国宝]]に指定されている『週刊朝日百科 日本の国宝』29号、朝日新聞社、[[1997年]]（[[平成]]9年）、pp.'''2''' - 281 - '''2''' - 283。 === その他の社殿 === * 御釜殿 *: [[江戸時代]]、[[慶長]]11年（[[1606年]]）の鉱山師・安原知種による再建。単層[[入母屋造]]の平入で、本瓦葺。南北に伸びた長方形で、北二間に釜を置く。金曜日を除く毎日、特殊神事の「[[鳴釜神事]]」が行われる。国の重要文化財に指定されている。 * 回廊 *: [[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]、[[天正]]年間（[[1573年]] - 応永8年（[[1401年]]）に吉備津神社で行われた法楽連歌の発句を集めたもの。1959年（昭和34年）3月27日指定[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=764 本墨書連歌] {{ja icon}}（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 * 無形民俗文化財 ** 宮内踊 - 門前町の宮内地区で[[7月31日]]に行われる。1959年（昭和34年）3月27日指定[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=435 宮内踊] {{ja icon}}（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 == 被害 == * [[2021年]]（[[令和]]3年）1月15日から22日にかけて、神社の拝殿や回廊の柱などに何者かが線状の傷をつけていたことが発覚。同年2月に[[松山城]]や[[高知城]]に傷をつけていた容疑者が[[文化財保護法]]違反で逮捕され、吉備津神社でも同様の犯行を行っていたとして再逮捕されている{{Cite web|和書|date=2021-02-13 |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210213122041/https://www.jiji.com/jc/article?k=2021021300375&g=soc |title=吉備津神社に傷付けた疑い　47歳男を再逮捕―岡山県警 |website=時事通信|publisher=時事通信社|accessdate=2021-02-13}} {{ja icon}}。 == 登場作品 == * 『[[雨月物語]]』 - 「吉備津の釜」にて[[鳴釜神事]]が登場する。 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[岡山県]][[岡山市]][[北区 (岡山市)|北区]]吉備津931 '''交通アクセス''' * 鉄道 ** [[西日本旅客鉄道]]（JR西日本）[[吉備線]] [[吉備津駅]] （徒歩10分） * バス **[[備北バス]]（[[東総社駅|東総社]]経由「地頭」行き）で、「吉備津神社参道口」バス停下車 （下車後、徒歩2分） **[[中鉄バス]]（[[国道180号]]方面「吉備津神社」行き）で、「吉備津神社」終点バス停下車 （下車後、徒歩すぐ）（現在休止中） **中鉄バス（国道180号方面「稲荷山」行き、または「大井行き」）で、「吉備津神社参道口」バス停下車 （下車後、徒歩2分）（現在{{いつ|date= 2025年6月21日 (土) 21:10 (UTC)}}休止中） '''周辺''' [[File:Nakayama Chausuyama Kofun, haisho.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|[[中山茶臼山古墳]]}}{{small|大吉備津彦命の宮内庁治定墓。}}]] * [[吉備の中山]] *: 境内後方の吉備の中山には多くの古墳や古代祭祀遺跡が残り、古くより[[神体山]]として信仰されたと考えられている。中央の茶臼山（160メートル）山頂には大吉備津彦命の墓とされる古墳があるほか、最高峰の竜王山（北峰、標高175メートル）山頂には吉備津彦神社が祀る[[磐座]]がある。 ** [[中山茶臼山古墳]] - 墳丘長120メートルの[[前方後円墳]]。宮内庁により「大吉備津彦命墓」として治定されている。 ** 吉備考古館 * [[吉備津彦神社]] - 備前国一宮。 * 伝賀陽氏館跡 - 吉備津神社神官を務めた[[賀陽氏]]の館跡とされる。岡山県の指定史跡[http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=325 伝賀陽氏館跡] {{ja icon}}（岡山県ホームページ「おかやまの文化財」）。。 * [[明菴栄西|栄西]]上人生誕地の碑 * [[造山古墳]] - 全国第4位の大きさの前方後円墳。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist|2}} == 参考文献 == * 谷川健一 編『日本の神々 -神社と聖地- 2 山陽 四国』（[[白水社]]）「吉備津神社項」 * 『[[日本歴史地名大系]] 岡山県の地名』（[[平凡社]]）「岡山市 吉備津神社項」 * 藤井学・山崎浩之編『改訂増補 備中吉備津神社文書 中世篇』（[[法藏館]]、[[2012年]]（平成24年）） == 関連項目 == * [[吉備津]] * [[吉備国]] * [[鬼ノ城]] * [[桃太郎]] * [[吉備津神社 (福山市)|吉備津神社]]（[[広島県]][[福山市]]新市町） - 備後国一宮。 == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat}} * [https://kibitujinja.com/ 吉備津神社 公式サイト]{{ja icon}} * [https://www.okayama-jinjacho.or.jp/search/18477/ 吉備津神社（岡山県神社庁）] {{ja icon}} * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/470101.html 吉備津彦神社（國學院大學21世紀COEプログラム「神道・神社史料集成」）] {{ja icon}} {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:きひつしんしや}} [[Category:岡山市の神社]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:備中国の式内社|名きひつしんしや]] [[Category:一宮]] [[Category:官幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:岡山県の国宝]] [[Category:日本の国宝 (建造物)]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:岡山市の重要文化財]] [[Category:室町時代の建築]] [[Category:備中国|社1]] [[Category:岡山市北区の建築物]] [[Category:岡山市北区の歴史]]

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Okayama Prefecture, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=November 2019}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Kibitsu Jinja
吉備津神社 | image = Kibitsu Jinja 10 cropped.jpg | caption = [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]] (1425), a [[National Treasures of Japan|National Treasure]] {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|14.4|N|133|51|2.2|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title, inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = Kibitsu Jinja | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 931 Kibitsu, Kita-ku, Okayama-shi, Okayama-ken 701-1341 | website = {{official|1=https://kibitujinja.com}} | architecture_style = | festivals = Second Sunday in May and October 15th each year | leadership = | footnotes = }} {{nihongo|'''Kibitsu Jinja'''|吉備津神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in the Kibitsu neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' (first shrine) of former [[Bitchū Province]]. The shrine’s main festivals are held on the second Sunday in May and October 15th each year.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} ==Overview== The Kibitsu Jinja is located in the western part of Okayama city, facing north at the northwestern foot of Mount Kibi-Nakayama (elevation 175 meters) on the border between former [[Bizen Province]] and Bitchū Province. The mountain has been worshipped as a [[sacred mountain]] from ancient times, and both the Kibitsu Jinja and [[Kibitsuhiko Shrine|Kibitsuhiko Jinja]] are located at its northeastern foot. Kibitsu Jinja was originally the general guardian of [[Kibi Province]], but due to the division of Kibi Province into three provinces, it became the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of Bitchū, and ''[[bunrei]]'' from this shrine created the ''ichinomiya'' of Bizen Province (Kibitsuhiko Jinja) and [[Bingo Province]] (Kibitsu Shrine). The [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]], which was re-built by [[Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]], is a [[National Treasures of Japan|National Treasure]] and the sole exemplar of the ''[[kibitsu-zukuri]]'' style of [[Japanese architecture|architecture]], although the [[Dō (architecture)|Soshidō]] of [[Hokekyō-ji (Ichikawa)|Hokekyō-ji]] is now believed to have been modeled thereon.{{cite web |url=http://www.aisf.or.jp/~jaanus/deta/k/kibitsuzukuri.htm |title=Kibitsu-zukuri |publisher=[[Japanese Architecture and Art Net Users System]] |access-date=4 May 2011}}{{cite book |title=Architectural Preservation in Japan |author=Larsen, Knut Einar |publisher=[[ICOMOS]] International Wood Committee |year=1994 |pages=121–5 |isbn=82-519-1432-9}} In addition, the three shrine buildings are designated as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]], and a special Shinto ritual "Narukama Shinto" is famous. === Mizuko and Sorei syncretism === The Shrine has a unique dual worship of [[Sorei]] or ancestral spirits alongside [[Mizuko kuyō]]{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=239}} or cults of miscarried babies. The shrine started as a place for the Kibi clan. It has the clan's ancestors as gods. This gives the shrine a pure and protective feel. The ancestors are seen as good and helpful spirits. This is how the shrine connects with [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] means the souls of babies who died early or were not born.{{Rp|page=239}} The shrine places the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] shrine next to the ancestor shrine. It also uses running water. This setup has several meanings:{{Rp|page=239}} # The water purifies the souls of [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] is linked to water.{{Rp|page=239}} # Being near the ancestor shrine suggests these souls become kind and protective spirits.{{Rp|page=239}} # As protective spirits, the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] guard those who remember them.{{Rp|page=239}} This way, the Kibitsu Shrine uses its ties to the Kibi clan. It creates a respectful place for [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. It links them to the shrine's ancestral and protective gods.{{Rp|page=239}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Kibitsu Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]]'''|吉備津彦命|}}, the son of [[Emperor Kōrei]] and conqueror of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]] and founder of the [[Kibi clan]] * {{nihongo|'''Mitomowake-no-mikoto'''| 御友別命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Nakatsuhiko-no-mikoto| 仲彦命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Chichihaya-hime-no-mikoto'''|千々速比売命|}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Yamato-totohimomoso-hime-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日百襲姫命 |}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosasukatawake-no-mikoto'''| 日子刺肩別命|}}, elder brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosashikatawake-no-mikoto'''| 彦刺肩別命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hiko same ma no mikoto'''|彦寤間命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Wakahiko Takekibitsu Hikono-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日稚屋媛命|}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko ==History== The origins of Kibitsu Jinja are uncertain. According to the shrine's legend, it is located at the site of Kibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto's residence, where he died at the age of 281, and was buried on the summit of the mountain. Afterwards, the residence was turned into a shrine, possibly by his fifth generation descendent Narumi Kaya, or by [[Emperor Nintoku]], who visited [[Kibi Province]] where he built several shrines to commemorate Kibitsuhiko. However, the shrine does not appear in any historical documentation until the late [[Heian period]], until entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihon Kōki]]'' dated 847 and the ''[[Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku]]'' dated 852. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'' it was given the Rank of {{nihongo|''Myojin Taisha''|名神大社||}} and the Rank of ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of the province. From the [[Kamakura period|Kamakura]] through the [[Sengoku period]], was revered by the samurai, and there were frequent restorations of the shrine and donations of territory. {{Citation needed|date=November 2023}} During the [[Edo period]], the shrine's land became smaller. However, it still got a special land grant from the shogunate. This grant was for 160 koku of rice every year. There was a busy market near the shrine. People also visited teahouses and inns there. Inside the shrine area, there was a theater and a brothel. The shrine was a busy place along the [[San'yōdō|San’yodō]] for travellers. This continued until the [[Meiji Restoration]]..{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=282}} After the [[Meiji Restoration]] in 1871, it was listed as a {{nihongo|National Shrine, 2nd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Chusha}}, and is 1914 was promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial Shrine, 2nd Rank|官幣中社|Kampei Chusha}}.{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese}}{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} The shrine is a ten-minute walk from [[Kibitsu Station]] on the [[JR West]] [[Kibi Line]]. ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *''[[Honden]]'' and ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]]'', [[Muromachi period]], built in 1390 and relocated their present locations in 1425.The main shrine has a ''Kibitsu-zukuri'' style roof, which consists of two [[East Asian hip-and-gable roof|''Irimoya-zukuri'']] roof are lined up in front and behind. The influence of Buddhist architecture can be seen in many details of the structure.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2993 |title= 吉備津神社本殿及び拝殿|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine main hall and worship hall|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} ===Important Cultural Properties=== *{{nihongo|'''South Zuishinmon'''|南随神門||}}, [[Muromachi period]], built in 1357.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2994 |title=吉備津神社南随神門|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine South Zuijinmon|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} *{{nihongo|'''North Zuishinmon'''|北随神門||}}, [[Sengoku period]], built in 1543.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2995 |title=吉備津神社北随神門|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine North Zuijinmon|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} *{{nihongo|'''Okama-den'''|御釜殿||}}, [[Edo period]], built in 1612.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2996 |title= 吉備津神社御釜殿|trans-title=Kibitsu Shrine Okamaden|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} *{{nihongo|'''Komainu'''|木造獅子狛犬||}}, one pair, late [[Kamakura Period|Kamakura]] to [[Nanboku-cho period]], Located to the east and west of the Honden.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/10545 |title= 木造獅子狛犬|trans-title=Mokuzō shishi komainu|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=August 20, 2020}} ==Gallery== File:吉備津神社 御釜殿.JPG|Okamaden（ICP） File:Kibitsu Jinja Corridor 03.JPG|Cloister File:吉備津神社 北随神門.JPG|North Zuijinmon（ICP） File:Kibitujinja5024.JPG|Approach and Ni-no-Torii File:吉備津神社 一の鳥居.JPG|Ichi-no-Torii ==See also== *[[List of National Treasures of Japan (shrines)]] *[[Ichinomiya]] *[[Hokekyō-ji (Ichikawa)]] ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons Category:11]] [[Category|Kibitsu Jinja}} *[https://kibitujinja.com Official home page] *[https://www.okayama-japan.jp/en/spot/782 Okayama prefecture Official Tourism Guide] {{Kibi clan}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{Ichinomiya}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages and Categories from It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' (first shrine) of former [[Bitchū Province]]. The shrine’s main festivals are held on the second Sunday in May and October 15th each year.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} ==Overview== The Kibitsu Jinja is located in the western part of Okayama city, facing north at the northwestern foot of Mount Kibi-Nakayama (elevation 175 meters) on the border between former [[Bizen Province]] and Bitchū Province. The mountain has been worshipped as a [[sacred mountain]] from ancient times, and both the Kibitsu Jinja and [[Kibitsuhiko Shrine|Kibitsuhiko Jinja]] are located at its northeastern foot. Kibitsu Jinja was originally the general guardian of [[Kibi Province]], but due to the division of Kibi Province into three provinces, it became the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of Bitchū, and ''[[bunrei]]'' from this shrine created the ''ichinomiya'' of Bizen Province (Kibitsuhiko Jinja) and [[Bingo Province]] (Kibitsu Shrine). The [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]], which was re-built by [[Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]], is a [[National Treasures of Japan|National Treasure]] and the sole exemplar of the ''[[kibitsu-zukuri]]'' style of [[Japanese architecture|architecture]], although the [[Dō (architecture)|Soshidō]] of [[Hokekyō-ji (Ichikawa)|Hokekyō-ji]] is now believed to have been modeled thereon.{{cite web |url=http://www.aisf.or.jp/~jaanus/deta/k/kibitsuzukuri.htm |title=Kibitsu-zukuri |publisher=[[Japanese Architecture and Art Net Users System]] |access-date=4 May 2011}}{{cite book |title=Architectural Preservation in Japan |author=Larsen, Knut Einar |publisher=[[ICOMOS]] International Wood Committee |year=1994 |pages=121–5 |isbn=82-519-1432-9}} In addition, the three shrine buildings are designated as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]], and a special Shinto ritual "Narukama Shinto" is famous. === Mizuko and Sorei syncretism === The Shrine has a unique dual worship of [[Sorei]] or ancestral spirits alongside [[Mizuko kuyō]]{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=239}} or cults of miscarried babies. The shrine started as a place for the Kibi clan. It has the clan's ancestors as gods. This gives the shrine a pure and protective feel. The ancestors are seen as good and helpful spirits. This is how the shrine connects with [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] means the souls of babies who died early or were not born.{{Rp|page=239}} The shrine places the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] shrine next to the ancestor shrine. It also uses running water. This setup has several meanings:{{Rp|page=239}} # The water purifies the souls of [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. It creates a respectful place for [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' (first shrine) of former [[Bitchū Province]]. The mountain has been worshipped as a [[sacred mountain]] from ancient times, and both the Kibitsu Jinja and [[Kibitsuhiko Shrine|Kibitsuhiko Jinja]] are located at its northeastern foot. Kibitsu Jinja was originally the general guardian of [[Kibi Province]], but due to the division of Kibi Province into three provinces, it became the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of Bitchū, and ''[[bunrei]]'' from this shrine created the ''ichinomiya'' of Bizen Province (Kibitsuhiko Jinja) and [[Bingo Province]] (Kibitsu Shrine). The [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]], which was re-built by [[Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]], is a [[National Treasures of Japan|National Treasure]] and the sole exemplar of the ''[[kibitsu-zukuri]]'' style of [[Japanese architecture|architecture]], although the [[Dō (architecture)|Soshidō]] of [[Hokekyō-ji (Ichikawa)|Hokekyō-ji]] is now believed to have been modeled thereon.{{cite web |url=http://www.aisf.or.jp/~jaanus/deta/k/kibitsuzukuri.htm |title=Kibitsu-zukuri |publisher=[[Japanese Architecture and Art Net Users System]] |access-date=4 May 2011}}{{cite book |title=Architectural Preservation in Japan |author=Larsen, Knut Einar |publisher=[[ICOMOS]] International Wood Committee |year=1994 |pages=121–5 |isbn=82-519-1432-9}} In addition, the three shrine buildings are designated as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]], and a special Shinto ritual "Narukama Shinto" is famous. === Mizuko and Sorei syncretism === The Shrine has a unique dual worship of [[Sorei]] or ancestral spirits alongside [[Mizuko kuyō]]{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=239}} or cults of miscarried babies. The shrine started as a place for the Kibi clan. It has the clan's ancestors as gods. This gives the shrine a pure and protective feel. The ancestors are seen as good and helpful spirits. This is how the shrine connects with [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] means the souls of babies who died early or were not born.{{Rp|page=239}} The shrine places the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] shrine next to the ancestor shrine. It also uses running water. This setup has several meanings:{{Rp|page=239}} # The water purifies the souls of [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. 吉備津神社 | image = Kibitsu Jinja 10 cropped.jpg | caption = [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]] (1425), a [[National Treasures of Japan|National Treasure]] {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|14.4|N|133|51|2.2|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title, inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = Kibitsu Jinja | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 931 Kibitsu, Kita-ku, Okayama-shi, Okayama-ken 701-1341 | website = {{official|1=https://kibitujinja.com}} | architecture_style = | festivals = Second Sunday in May and October 15th each year | leadership = | footnotes = }} {{nihongo|'''Kibitsu Jinja'''|吉備津神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in the Kibitsu neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]] in [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' (first shrine) of former [[Bitchū Province]]. The shrine’s main festivals are held on the second Sunday in May and October 15th each year.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} ==Overview== The Kibitsu Jinja is located in the western part of Okayama city, facing north at the northwestern foot of Mount Kibi-Nakayama (elevation 175 meters) on the border between former [[Bizen Province]] and Bitchū Province. The mountain has been worshipped as a [[sacred mountain]] from ancient times, and both the Kibitsu Jinja and [[Kibitsuhiko Shrine|Kibitsuhiko Jinja]] are located at its northeastern foot. Kibitsu Jinja was originally the general guardian of [[Kibi Province]], but due to the division of Kibi Province into three provinces, it became the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of Bitchū, and ''[[bunrei]]'' from this shrine created the ''ichinomiya'' of Bizen Province (Kibitsuhiko Jinja) and [[Bingo Province]] (Kibitsu Shrine). The [[Honden]]-[[Haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]], which was re-built by [[Ashikaga Yoshimitsu]], is a [[National Treasures of Japan|National Treasure]] and the sole exemplar of the ''[[kibitsu-zukuri]]'' style of [[Japanese architecture|architecture]], although the [[Dō (architecture)|Soshidō]] of [[Hokekyō-ji (Ichikawa)|Hokekyō-ji]] is now believed to have been modeled thereon.{{cite web |url=http://www.aisf.or.jp/~jaanus/deta/k/kibitsuzukuri.htm |title=Kibitsu-zukuri |publisher=[[Japanese Architecture and Art Net Users System]] |access-date=4 May 2011}}{{cite book |title=Architectural Preservation in Japan |author=Larsen, Knut Einar |publisher=[[ICOMOS]] International Wood Committee |year=1994 |pages=121–5 |isbn=82-519-1432-9}} In addition, the three shrine buildings are designated as National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]], and a special Shinto ritual "Narukama Shinto" is famous. === Mizuko and Sorei syncretism === The Shrine has a unique dual worship of [[Sorei]] or ancestral spirits alongside [[Mizuko kuyō]]{{Cite book |last=Hardacre |first=Helen |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nunQEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Kibi+clan%22&pg=PA239 |title=Marketing the Menacing Fetus in Japan |date=2023-09-01 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-92204-4 |language=en}}{{Rp|page=239}} or cults of miscarried babies. The shrine started as a place for the Kibi clan. It has the clan's ancestors as gods. This gives the shrine a pure and protective feel. The ancestors are seen as good and helpful spirits. This is how the shrine connects with [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] means the souls of babies who died early or were not born.{{Rp|page=239}} The shrine places the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] shrine next to the ancestor shrine. It also uses running water. This setup has several meanings:{{Rp|page=239}} # The water purifies the souls of [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. [[Mizuko kuyō|Mizuko]] is linked to water.{{Rp|page=239}} # Being near the ancestor shrine suggests these souls become kind and protective spirits.{{Rp|page=239}} # As protective spirits, the [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]] guard those who remember them.{{Rp|page=239}} This way, the Kibitsu Shrine uses its ties to the Kibi clan. It creates a respectful place for [[Mizuko kuyō|mizuko]]. It links them to the shrine's ancestral and protective gods.{{Rp|page=239}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Kibitsu Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto]]'''|吉備津彦命|}}, the son of [[Emperor Kōrei]] and conqueror of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]] and founder of the [[Kibi clan]] * {{nihongo|'''Mitomowake-no-mikoto'''| 御友別命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Nakatsuhiko-no-mikoto| 仲彦命|}}, descendant of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Chichihaya-hime-no-mikoto'''|千々速比売命|}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Yamato-totohimomoso-hime-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日百襲姫命 |}}, elder sister of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosasukatawake-no-mikoto'''| 日子刺肩別命|}}, elder brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hikosashikatawake-no-mikoto'''| 彦刺肩別命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Hiko same ma no mikoto'''|彦寤間命 |}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko * {{nihongo|'''Wakahiko Takekibitsu Hikono-no-mikoto'''| 倭迹迹日稚屋媛命|}}, brother of Kibitsuhiko ==History== The origins of Kibitsu Jinja are uncertain.
